independent_cross_reviews.selection_rationale: A well-targeted diagnostic for distinguishing the wearer and the wearer-associated objects from other people and visually similar objects. Human-authored questions and comparison of open-ended with multiple-choice answers add credible marginal value. It is especially relevant before building worker-specific memory, while its temporal horizon and oracle analysis sharply limit claims of durable memory.
corrected_or_qualified_claims: Main evaluation is causal to the question timestamp: uniform sampling uses only the video prefix, usually 32 frames and at most 1 fps. LongVA/LongVU receive 128 frames, so comparisons across those models are not frame-matched.

Table 3 is an oracle evidence-availability experiment. It uses known answer and question moments, eight frames within ±1.5 seconds around each. The paper does not clearly state whether the positive offset around the question is clipped. Do not present this as a deployable or proven causal retrieval gain.

The Table 3 uniform baseline differs slightly from Table 2 for several open models. Quote Table 3 pairs together rather than subtracting across tables. Gemini Previous is 40.3 to 51.5, while Qwen2.5 is 33.2 to 42.4.

Human 84.7 open-ended accuracy is from 300 questions answered by two university students, rather than the full 5,012-question model evaluation. The numerical full-table gap is therefore descriptive rather than a matched estimate.
Ninety percent of answer-to-query intervals are below 40 seconds. The nine-minute average source video does not imply that the questions test nine-minute or shift-long retention.

Prompt effects are small and mixed. Table 4 includes declines under the enhanced prompt and an improvement after removing personalization cues. Avoid a general claim that enhanced prompting reliably solves ego-grounding.

candidates.title: Bridging Modalities, Spanning Time: Structured Memory for Ultra-Long Agentic Video Reasoning
candidates.reason: Deferred first note: another rich graph/narrative memory. Compare against the simpler MERIT and WorldMM before adding a third graph stack.

candidates.title: APM-Bench: Benchmarking Cross-session Persistent Memory for Egocentric Streaming Video Assistants
candidates.reason: Deferred first batch: cross-session interruption evaluation is useful after basic state/location and evidence acquisition testing is established.

candidates.title: EgoGraph: Temporal Knowledge Graph for Egocentric Video Understanding
candidates.reason: Deferred first batch: overlaps entity/time graph baselines WorldMM and EGAgent. Only abstract screened, no implementation or cost audit.

candidates.title: StreamForest: Efficient Online Video Understanding with Persistent Event Memory
candidates.reason: Deferred first batch: retained visual-token trees address model inference context, while initial pipeline needs an independently inspectable archive.

candidates.title: EgoProbe: Benchmarking Long-Range and Exact Memory in Streaming Egocentric Videos
candidates.reason: Deferred first batch: event attribution evaluation is relevant but would add another benchmark before implementing core retrieval.

candidates.title: EgoMemReason: A Memory-Driven Reasoning Benchmark for Long-Horizon Egocentric Video Understanding
candidates.reason: Deferred first batch: additional multi-day state/order benchmark. Core evaluation already includes ProactEgoMem plus upstream EgoLife.

candidates.title: EgoMonth: A Month-Level Egocentric Video Benchmark for Long-Term Spatiotemporal Memory
candidates.reason: Deferred first batch: calendar-span stress testing is useful later, but it does not establish continuous months of helmet-camera coverage.

candidates.title: VideoARM: Agentic Reasoning over Hierarchical Memory for Long-Form Video Understanding
candidates.reason: Deferred first batch: useful hierarchical tool-using predecessor, overlapping WorldMM and MERIT retrieval comparisons.

candidates.title: SCOUT: Self-Checking and Recovery-Aware Tool-Thought Agents for Ultra-Long Egocentric Video Reasoning
candidates.reason: Reader training is a follow-up once basic ingestion and retrieval work.

candidates.title: FluxMem: Adaptive Hierarchical Memory for Streaming Video Understanding
candidates.reason: Internal inference cache rather than independent persistent evidence memory.

candidates.title: Video Streaming Thinking: VideoLLMs Can Watch and Think Simultaneously
candidates.reason: Overlaps OneStreamer and StreamArena while answering a different online response timing objective.

candidates.title: StreamPro: From Reactive Perception to Proactive Decision-Making in Streaming Video
candidates.reason: Prioritize after task monitoring requirement and false-alarm evaluation are defined.

candidates.title: ProV-Mem: Proactive Memory for Streaming Video Question Answering
candidates.reason: Deferred: proactive notification memory overlaps OneStreamer. It does not directly supply a complete evidence archive.

candidates.title: Video-MemComp: Taylor-Guided Sensitivity-Aware Memory Management for Streaming Video Understanding
candidates.reason: Deferred: KV-cache compression is an inference optimization, not an independently queryable persistent memory.

candidates.title: Memory as Weights: Internalizing Long-Term History for Streaming Videos
candidates.reason: Deferred: implicit weight memory is less auditable than evidence records and needs model-training evaluation before pipeline adoption.

candidates.title: CapMem: A Benchmark for Caption-Based Episodic Memory in Egocentric Video
candidates.reason: Deferred additional benchmark while ProactEgoMem tests state/location acquisition and MemLife/CFD test writer/verification designs.

candidates.title: Ego-R1: Chain-of-Tool-Thought for Ultra-Long Egocentric Video Reasoning
candidates.reason: Deferred full note until reader training is needed. It remains a real citation predecessor, not an unrelated paper.

candidates.title: HippoMM: Hippocampal-inspired Multimodal Memory for Long Audiovisual Event Understanding
candidates.reason: Deferred because WorldMM/MERIT offer a more direct first implementation comparison. v2 adds authors compared with v1.

candidates.title: LVMH: A Meta-Optimization Harness for Long-Video Agent Memory
candidates.reason: Meta-optimization is a later stage once a baseline archive and evaluation set exist. Claimed savings need full cost-scope audit.

candidates.title: Pre-Decoding Acoustic Triage for Budgeted Vision-Language Captioning of Untrimmed Egocentric Video
candidates.reason: Coverage is any temporal overlap, not complete step or defect evidence. Ego4D metric is acoustic-moment retention, not action recall. Caption tests only200 stimuli and no factuality score.

candidates.title: Coarse Indexing, Fine Evidence: Decoupling Temporal Granularity in Long-Video RAG
candidates.reason: Deferred until a graph baseline is selected. Generic long-video evaluation, no worker-state/defect recall audit.

candidates.title: Have I Scene This Before? Spatially Grounded Conversational Memory for Complex Queries in Egocentric Assistants
candidates.reason: ScanNet sessions augmented with conversations address spatial dialogue grounding. Transfer to dynamic worker state histories remains unverified.

candidates.title: CUE-Mem: Benchmarking Long-Term User Memory via Implicit Cues in Multimodal Conversations
candidates.reason: The EMIR² lead supplied this ID, but the primary page is CUE-Mem. Identity mismatch rejected. Conversation memory is outside this video-first batch.

candidates.title: Beyond the Timeline: Augmenting Long-Video Memory with Grounded Entity Biographies
candidates.reason: Promising identity layer, but full-text association failure/cost analysis not checked. Start with LEDGER plus caption baseline before adding another tracking stack.

candidates.title: Imprint: Online Memory Compression for Long-Horizon Egocentric QA
candidates.reason: Retention biases may discard rare defects. Abstract-only, overlaps selected memory writer and retrieval comparisons.

candidates.title: Visual Agentic Memory: Enabling Online Long Video Understanding via Online Indexing, Hierarchical Memory, and Agentic Retrieval
candidates.reason: Month-scale result remains low and OVO gain over same backbone is small. Full-text fairness/cost not checked. StreamArena covers first system comparison.

candidates.title: Graph it first! Enabling Reasoning on Long-form Egocentric Videos through Scene Graphs
candidates.reason: Potentially useful, but full text required to audit source annotations and extraction. Overlaps selected graph memories.

candidates.title: EgoMemory: Memory-Augmented Personalized Retrieval for Long-Context Egocentric Video
candidates.reason: Personalized episodic retrieval benchmark. Defer until user-specific memory is needed, rather than objective work-evidence retrieval.

candidates.title: Multi-Agent Egocentric World Model with Fine-Grained Embodied Interaction

foundation_search.status: All 10 selected PDFs and notes integrated in the 30-note expansion. Human review pending.
foundation_search.scope: Primarily 2021–2024, with two explicitly justified earlier conceptual roots. Curated for Aligned, not a universal physical-AI top ten.
criteria: Verified primary identity and original contribution
Concrete downstream adoption or acknowledged lineage
No duplicate slot for the same paper/version
foundation_search.reading_scope: Ten research passes used primary metadata, targeted original method/protocol sections, and actual downstream-paper passages. Reading depth varies. These are selection checks, not complete note audits or experimental reproductions.

recommendations: Ten-work core, with R3M as first reserve

selection.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning from Human Preferences
selection.role: Preference-derived reward learning scaled to deep RL.
selection.verified_lineage: FPL §§2–3.1 and §5.2 explicitly establish the conceptual lineage and scalar-preference comparison.
selection.status: PDF archived and note integrated, human review pending

selection.title: Who’s Better? Who’s Best? Pairwise Deep Ranking for Skill Determination
selection.role: Generic physical skill as relative ranking of video demonstrations.
selection.verified_lineage: ProSkill §2/Table 1 cites the conceptual/dataset predecessor. Its implemented RAAN baseline is the 2019 follow-up, not this method.
selection.status: PDF archived and note integrated, human review pending

selection.title: Ego4D: Around the World in 3,000 Hours of Egocentric Video
selection.role: Querying past wearable experience and localizing visual evidence.
selection.status: PDF archived and note integrated, human review pending

selection.title: Assembly101: A Large-Scale Multi-View Video Dataset for Understanding Procedural Activities
selection.role: Assembly procedures, flexible action order, mistakes and corrections.
selection.verified_lineage: ProSkill §4 uses 560 clips across 35 actions from Assembly101.
selection.status: PDF archived and note integrated, human review pending

selection.title: Look for the Change: Learning Object States and State-Modifying Actions from Untrimmed Web Videos
selection.role: Initial state, modifying action and resulting state as learning targets.
selection.verified_lineage: VidOSC §2/Table 2 reuses ChangeIt and compares LookForTheChange. MOSCATO cites the predecessor but does not evaluate ChangeIt.
selection.status: PDF archived and note integrated, human review pending

selection.title: VIP: Towards Universal Visual Reward and Representation via Value-Implicit Pre-Training
selection.role: Goal-image visual rewards learned from passive human video.
selection.verified_lineage: PROGRESSOR §§5.2.2–5.2.3 pretrains and freezes VIP for a reward-weighted ACT comparison.
selection.status: PDF archived and note integrated, human review pending

selection.title: Ego-Exo4D: Understanding Skilled Human Activity from First- and Third-Person Perspectives
selection.role: Distinguishes person-level proficiency from timestamped execution feedback.
selection.verified_lineage: SkillSpotter §§1–2 adopts the proficiency-demonstration task. ProSkill uses bike-repair clips.
selection.status: PDF archived and note integrated, human review pending

selection.title: Error Detection in Egocentric Procedural Task Videos
selection.role: EgoPER normal-only mistake detection and its benchmark.
selection.verified_lineage: AEM §3.1 adopts the one-class setting and §4.1 evaluates EgoPER. AMNAR addresses prototype-method limitations.
selection.status: PDF archived and note integrated, human review pending

selection.title: AMEGO: Active Memory from long EGOcentric videos
selection.role: Reusable, query-independent memory of object interactions and activity locations.
selection.verified_lineage: LEDGER §4/Appendix B rebuilds AMEGO as an adapted baseline, rather than reproducing every original protocol.
selection.status: PDF archived and note integrated, human review pending

selection.title: VideoAgent: A Memory-augmented Multimodal Agent for Video Understanding
selection.role: Separates persistent event/object memory from LLM tool-based answering.
selection.verified_lineage: AMEGO §2, EGAgent related work and WorldMM §1 discuss this exact Fan et al. design. Embodied VideoAgent extends the line. Current citations do not establish code reuse.
selection.status: PDF archived and note integrated, human review pending

reserves.title: R3M
reserves.reason: First reserve for reusable human-video features. VIP occupies the current representation-to-reward slot. The methods are distinct.

reserves.title: EgoVLP
reserves.reason: Strong independent-review recommendation for retrieval and proficiency features. A next backbone read, beyond the current ten-role cap.

reserves.title: CaptainCook4D
reserves.reason: Strong independent-review recommendation and actual AEM/PROVIA benchmark. EgoPER takes the initial mistake slot because it contributes both a direct method ancestor and a benchmark.

reserves.title: IndustReal
reserves.reason: Correct step-completion evaluation is relevant, but an additional narrow assembly dataset would crowd out method foundations.

reserves.title: PEBBLE
reserves.reason: Feedback-efficient off-policy successor. Keep behind the conceptual preference root for this first historical layer.

reserves.title: Diffusion Policy
reserves.reason: Strongest policy-method reserve, with actual code/baseline reuse. Read when choosing the robot policy pipeline.

reserves.title: RLPD
reserves.reason: Core optimizer used by HIL-SERL, already covered in RL-Wiki. Lower current priority than worker-video memory and assessment.

reserves.title: ACT / ALOHA
reserves.reason: Directly adapted by PROGRESSOR, but action-labeled robot demonstrations are a later pipeline concern.

reserves.title: SCHEMA
reserves.reason: Direct AEM inspiration. Look for the Change fills the earlier state-change foundation slot.

reserves.title: OSNOM
reserves.reason: 2024 preprint, 3DV2025. Already archived, direct LEDGER comparison. A later spatial-persistence read.

reserves.title: EMQA
reserves.reason: Earlier spatial-memory formulation, with less verified downstream adoption than the selected memory pair.

reserves.title: EPIC-KITCHENS-100
reserves.reason: 2020 preprint, online journal2021, volume2022. Important shared infrastructure, but lower priority than three distinct selected task/data roots.

cautions: Two VideoAgent papers appeared at ECCV2024. The selection is Fan et al., arXiv2403.11481, not Wang et al., arXiv2403.10517.
Christiano2017 scaled preference feedback to deep RL and explicitly credits earlier preference-learning work. It did not invent preference learning.
FPL attributes PPO to Christiano2017. The original uses A2C/TRPO. PPO appears in a later PEBBLE reimplementation.
ProSkill cites Who's Better2018 but implements the RAAN2019 follow-up as a baseline.
VidOSC reuses ChangeIt and compares LookForTheChange. MOSCATO cites the precursor and explicitly does not evaluate ChangeIt.
LEDGER rebuilds/adapts AMEGO. Its comparison must not be presented as a faithful reproduction of the original AMEGO system.
Pin source versions during later ingestion. Ego-Exo4D has a later journal expansion and Diffusion Policy changes author lists in later versions.

supplement_findings.finding: The LaViLa+ViCLIP and Ego4D+ViCLIP NLQ similarity ensembles use video-text:text-text ratios 18:11 and 7:8. These weights were chosen by grid search on the Ego4D NLQ training set using the four reported recall metrics.

supplement_findings.finding: Object memory querying is a separate GPT-4 SQL-writing agent. It has database_querying and open_vocabulary_retrieval tools, then returns a natural-language answer to the central GPT-4 controller.
supplement_findings.effect: Current note is broadly correct but can explicitly name the separate memory agent.

supplement_findings.location: Supplement D.1–D.3 and D.5, printed pp.24–29 and 31–34
supplement_findings.finding: Several author-labeled successful cases contain substantially incorrect Video-LLaVA descriptions. Case1 invents a parked airplane and opening its door, while the controller maps that account to the correct option 'moves away'. Case2 describes archery in a bat question. Case3 recognizes a ring while incorrectly describing the action as rock-paper-scissors. Case5 repeatedly reports incorrect ingredients or scenes before selecting the correct option.
supplement_findings.effect: A correct multiple-choice answer does not establish a faithful visual account or reliably grounded explanation. This is directly supported by the published traces and the authors' acknowledgements, not a new error-rate estimate.

supplement_findings.finding: Re-ID greedily merges tracks only when they never share a frame, all pair similarities to the group exceed0.5, and at least one exceeds0.62. Otherwise it creates a new identity.
supplement_findings.effect: Supports the existing appearance-based identity account. Does not establish physical-state modeling, transformation-robust identity, or streaming causality.

supplement_findings.finding: Reported comparison settings differ in access and backbone. ViperGPT uses GPT-3.5 and four uniformly sampled frames, while VideoAgent uses GPT-4 with memory built from the full video. Other fixed budgets are32 input/4 key frames for SeViLA,8 for Video-LLaVA and5 for mPLUG-Owl.
supplement_findings.effect: Treat aggregate QA improvement as system-level evidence, not a controlled isolation of memory architecture alone. Existing ablation remains the more direct memory evidence.

supplement_findings.finding: No additional systematic cost study, user deployment, state-change benchmark, or causal online-ingestion evaluation appears. The supplement adds implementation details and selected examples rather than changing the staged headline benchmark numbers.
supplement_findings.effect: Retain current limitations on comprehensive ingestion/query cost, deployment and physical-state tracking. No new practical-evidence tags justified.

cross_note_consistency.assessment: AMEGO tracks manipulated instances and contextual locations. LEDGER stores 3D resting segments and visibility gaps. Incremental graph updates, query-time prefix filtering, and offline full-trajectory preprocessing must remain distinct. Report ingestion plus query, rather than query tokens alone. GPU-only energy is not device-wide energy. Throughput under parallel workers is not per-query latency.

EgoExoLearn offers comparative skill judgments. EgoExoBench reference-removal controls demonstrate shortcut risks. EgoTaskQA provides symbolic task dependencies with language shortcuts. Multi-Ego evaluates subjective highlights. None establishes construction-worker competence.

ranked_shortlist_within_assignment.caveat: Large solver, limited retrieval hit rate, 500-question EgoLife test, and initial caption cost excluded from construction accounting. Practical means easiest controlled starting experiment here, not production readiness.

ranked_shortlist_within_assignment.why: Persistent interaction tracks, timestamps and visual descriptors preserve information caption text can omit. Distinct role earns a second memory slot.
ranked_shortlist_within_assignment.caveat: Interaction detector assumptions and same-category different-instance filtering limit identity evidence. It is not 3D metrology or defect detection.

ranked_shortlist_within_assignment.caveat: Cooking-centered short clips, modest/mixed reference gains and no verified worker/site-disjoint construction generalization.

ranked_shortlist_within_assignment.why: Distinct coverage of questions requiring information across people, beyond independent personal memory. Actual construction/retrieval code exists.

cross_note_consistency: EgoPER is a normal-only anomaly/error baseline under its own protocol. AMNAR extends valid next-action branches. AEM changes emphasis toward visual local action effects. Cross-paper improvements do not imply matched supervision, and AEM does not uniformly beat AMNAR.
AEM CaptainCook mistake EDA71.9 is below AMNAR72.3 despite better precision/AUC. Prefer AEM for distinct outcome-sensitive supervision, not universal dominance.

MistSense, MATT, STORM-PSR and AEM use incompatible mistake definitions, temporal visibility and supervision. Do not compare their headline accuracy as one ranking. MistSense Holo error precision10.3 and STORM true-positive-conditioned delays are important qualifiers.

IndEgo dataset industrial and collaborative recordings are relevant domain evidence. IndEgo Assistant evaluates offline recordings in one disassembly scenario, not a field deployment, user trial or demonstrated worker productivity benefit.

Ego4D and Ego-Exo4D corpus hours are aggregate capture across many people, not one continuous personal-memory horizon. EM²Mem44.3h and GEBapproximately52h use different processing/version protocols over one wearer, not independent multiworker evidence.

EM²Mem coverage gains and GEB identity-association coverage gains do not entail significant or even visible mean answer-score gains. Evidence retrieval, identity correctness and answer correctness must remain separate.

OSNOM persistent 3D positions use full-video reconstruction and retrospective backfill. GEB descriptions use surrounding/future text and consolidated profiles. Neither establishes strictly causal online memory.

ProSkill and EgoExoLearn labels estimate perceived skill for clips, not certified construction quality or participant-disjoint professional competence. ExpertAF generates useful critiques without a controlled downstream skill-improvement trial.

ranked_spotlight_recommendation.role: Industrial and collaborative worker-camera evaluation substrate
ranked_spotlight_recommendation.why: Closest assigned dataset to actual worker procedures, errors, gaze/audio and collaboration. Includes real limitations in multimodal robustness and annotation reliability.
ranked_spotlight_recommendation.nearest_alternative: Prefer over Ego-Exo4D for industrial error/collaboration evaluation. Ego-Exo4D is larger and better suited to expertise and explanatory commentary. EgoExoLearn is stronger for pairwise comparative skill and asynchronous demonstrations, not industrial error coverage.
ranked_spotlight_recommendation.limitation: Controlled procedures and supplied segments/known mistake prompts. Not proof of field monitoring or business impact.

ranked_spotlight_recommendation.why: Adds object state and local action-effect supervision rather than judging only the next action sequence. External models distill training supervision, avoiding those calls at inference.
ranked_spotlight_recommendation.nearest_alternative: Prefer over AMNAR for a scarce slot because outcome quality is a distinct requirement. AMNAR remains a valid-order/branching baseline and wins one reported CaptainCook EDA comparison72.3vs71.9.
ranked_spotlight_recommendation.limitation: Correct-video/action supervision, imperfect generated graph supervision, local effects not long-range job completion. Small scene-graph checks are not reliable quality certification.

ranked_spotlight_recommendation.role: Foundational normal-only error protocol and taxonomy
ranked_spotlight_recommendation.why: Concrete released baseline and scripted-error dataset help define training on correct demonstrations, abnormal execution and step-level outputs.
ranked_spotlight_recommendation.nearest_alternative: Retain alongside IndEgo only if spotlight can afford foundational baseline plus industrial evaluation. It adds protocol clarity, while IndEgo adds domain/collaboration. It is not another general skill-score dataset like Ego-Exo4D/EgoExoLearn.
ranked_spotlight_recommendation.limitation: Cooking, few people/environments, scripted errors, offline processing and some labeled errors without failed outcomes.

ranked_spotlight_recommendation.role: Provenance-preserving event memory and complete cost accounting
ranked_spotlight_recommendation.why: Most controlled assigned evidence for binding modalities before retrieval, with confidence intervals separating coverage from uncertain QA. Complete construction-plus500-query token totals constrain cheap-indexing claims.
ranked_spotlight_recommendation.nearest_alternative: Prefer over EgoCITE for isolated representation evidence and transparent total costs. WorldMM remains predecessor. GEB offers complementary physical identity but poorer immediate release/cost readiness.
ranked_spotlight_recommendation.limitation: Single wearer, offline global summaries/facts. Throughput advantages partly parallel execution. Higher total token count at tested workload.

ranked_spotlight_recommendation.role: Inspectable baseline for out-of-view object-location memory
ranked_spotlight_recommendation.why: Persistent 3D object locations give a distinct spatial component for locating tools/materials across occlusion. Released implementation and explicit error/time horizons support concrete evaluation.
ranked_spotlight_recommendation.nearest_alternative: More direct location-memory component than GEB biography QA. AMEGO from the other assignment may offer a simpler appearance/interaction memory baseline. Choose between them based on whether geometry is required.
ranked_spotlight_recommendation.limitation: Whole-video geometry, costly reconstruction, retrospective updates and interpolated ground truth. Association speed excludes perception.

alternative_spotlight_slots.recommendation: Strong optional slot if proof-of-skill annotation deserves its own place. Its Swiss tournament and consensus recipe is more directly reusable for annotation workflow than broad Ego-Exo4D expertise proxies. EgoExoLearn is the nearest complementary pairwise-skill benchmark, with clearer controlled reference/gaze comparisons. ProSkill remains perceived skill and may reward visible fluency over objective outcomes.

Do not spend a scarce evidence/field-validation slot on it. Include only to illustrate explicit human approval of procedure onboarding and reusable graph/state interface. Later code is a reference implementation. No UI, latency or live-user benefit evaluated.

alternative_spotlight_slots.role: Foundation for expert critique and expertise-linked data
alternative_spotlight_slots.recommendation: Useful foundation, but not automatically another top slot when IndEgo plus EgoPER already cover evaluation data. Distinct strength is expert commentary and synchronized viewpoints, not direct construction competence labels.
Include when explaining field milestones and NLQ/state tasks, but product shortlist can cite its influence without spending a slot if more specific evaluation principles cover it.

cross_note_consistency: SkillSpotter measures localization of feedback moments and grading conditioned on matched detections. FLORA annotates segments and provides quality/reward outputs. PROVIA evaluates full-trial causal alarms, recovery and false-alarm budgets. Their results must not be ranked as one skill metric.

S-EMBER tests answer-plus-interval grounding over minutes. EgoMemReason tests multi-day evidence aggregation in the shared EgoLife environment. SuperMemory-VQA adds multiple-choice abstention and speech-linked intent with a smaller partly scripted collection. These are complementary evaluation axes.
EGOSTREAM and EgoProbe motivate validity and repeated-event tests, but their current protocol/release limitations make them secondary to the two stronger memory evaluators.

VidParse normal-video segmentation, PRISM post-completion error reasoning and PROVIA supervised streaming alarms have different annotation assumptions and deployment access. None demonstrates general construction workmanship.

FPL uses supervised score-conditioned policy learning. RoboReward, Robometer, ReWiND and HIL-SERL report distinct robot-learning protocols. Their robot success numbers do not establish human skill assessment or passive-video reward reliability.

ranked_spotlight_recommendations.why: The closest assigned work to a camera-based, human-reviewed quality workflow. It separates locating a review moment from grading its execution and exposes weak subtle-manipulation categories.
ranked_spotlight_recommendations.limit: Offline context and pose are required. Matched-detection accuracy ignores missed moments.
ranked_spotlight_recommendations.alternative: FLORA provides broader annotation outputs but has a small dense failure test and weaker human-feedback alignment.

ranked_spotlight_recommendations.role: Evaluate full executions and operational false alarms
ranked_spotlight_recommendations.why: Distinct evaluation discipline for recoveries, deferred/corrected errors, timing controls and false alarms over complete trials. Its low recall at a strict false-alarm budget is useful evidence of the remaining problem.
ranked_spotlight_recommendations.limit: Preprint, supervised segmentation/status labels, controlled baseline simplifications and no construction field trial.
ranked_spotlight_recommendations.alternative: PRISM supplies transparent offline controls but assumes gold segments and known references. TGML is useful structural machinery, with recognition and cycle limits.

ranked_spotlight_recommendations.why: Direct match to durable worker memory. Independent second-stage source review and oracle-evidence comparisons help expose retrieval and reasoning bottlenecks.
ranked_spotlight_recommendations.limit: Only 500 questions from one six-person shared environment, unequal model budgets and a released option-mapping correction.
ranked_spotlight_recommendations.alternative: SuperMemory-VQA adds abstention but has a smaller partly scripted collection. EgoProbe exposes binding errors with weaker current controls.

ranked_spotlight_recommendations.role: Require answers to point to supporting video intervals
ranked_spotlight_recommendations.why: A broad wearer pool and joint answer/localization metric provide a concrete evidence-grounding evaluator. It complements the longer-horizon benchmark.
ranked_spotlight_recommendations.limit: Minutes rather than days, prefix rereading, two-pass compute and gated non-commercial data.
ranked_spotlight_recommendations.alternative: EgoMemReason has the longer horizon but a smaller environment. Neither is a production memory architecture.

ranked_spotlight_recommendations.role: Released annotation and scoring component to prototype
ranked_spotlight_recommendations.why: Concrete segmentation/caption/reward outputs and released sample inference make it a plausible component candidate. It can connect event logs with candidate quality labels for human review.
ranked_spotlight_recommendations.limit: Only 40 dense failure-test episodes, 53.3% failure recall and about 11% normal false positives. Reported cost savings are modeled and internal production use is author-reported.
ranked_spotlight_recommendations.alternative: Use as a secondary practical candidate in the global shortlist if source-grounded retrieval and evaluation already occupy most slots. It should not replace PROVIA for alarm evaluation or SkillSpotter for review-moment selection.

candidates_views.secondary_reading: FPL is the next preference/rubric reference and HIL-SERL the later physical-policy example. They should remain secondary under the user’s current worker-camera, memory and quality focus.

spotlight_review.scope: Read all ten spotlight rows and the reading/product path against current cards. Used fresh final source receipts for the assigned cards and available other-agent receipts. Re-read exact MERIT sections 3.2 and Appendix A. Freshly rendered and inspected MA-EgoQA Figure 9 on PDF page 14 to distinguish paper presentation defects from verified release-label errors. factual_findings.location: MERIT spotlight, Why it earns a spotlight
factual_findings.observed_issue: “Final visual verification” can imply a distinct verification stage or visually verified retrieval stopping. The retrieval loop and sufficiency judgments use text only. Retrieved frames enter the final QA call.
factual_findings.source_evidence: Exact MERIT PDF section 3.2, p. 7 and Appendix A, p. 19. Appendix A explicitly says frames are input exclusively during final QA.
factual_findings.minimal_correction: Replace “final visual verification” with “final answering from retrieved frames”.

factual_findings.observed_issue: “Benchmark examples contain documented inconsistencies” is defensible but could be read as a verified error in the released benchmark labels. The concrete evidence checked here concerns the paper’s illustrated examples.
factual_findings.source_evidence: Fresh visual inspection of exact MA-EgoQA PDF Figure 9, p. 14: option C is bold, D is marked incorrect for two baselines and correct for EgoMAS. Earlier candidate receipt also identifies duplicated options in Table S2. Released example labels were not independently audited.
factual_findings.minimal_correction: Use “The paper’s illustrated examples contain reporting inconsistencies.”

quantitative_checks: EgoExoLearn 34,239 is retained comparisons, not people. Asynchronous demonstrations and mixed expert-reference gains are accurately retained.
MERIT retrieval hit rate 0.56, 500-question EgoLifeQA scope and omitted initial captioning cost are stated with appropriate limitations.
S-EMBER 5–20-minute clips and 64 plus 128 processed frames are correct. EgoMemReason has 500 questions and six people, with unequal budgets and option-letter revision correctly stated.
AEM 73.8 versus 86.7 AUC concerns predicted versus oracle EgoPER segments. The draft does not incorrectly present those as two equivalent end-to-end methods.
SkillSpotter weakness on subtle cooking/music moments, pose/offline access and matched-detection grading caveat are accurate.

selection_assessment.overall: The ten works cover the requested workers, memory and execution-quality focus. The roles are sufficiently distinct, and the reading path keeps robot policy learning secondary. S-EMBER and EgoMemReason both earn places because grounding over minutes and aggregation across days answer different evaluation questions.
selection_assessment.recommended_adjustment: Expand to eleven by adding PROVIA, rather than treating ten as a quota. It supplies the missing full-execution alarm protocol: recoveries, time-based shortcuts and false alarms across the whole trial. Low practical recall is the reason to use its protocol, not grounds to portray its detector as ready.

proposed_provia_row.why: Evaluate complete executions, recoveries and false alarms, with timing-only controls. Useful for deciding whether a quality alert remains trustworthy across the whole trial.
proposed_provia_row.limit: Fresh preprint with supervised segmentation/status labels and simplified baselines. Recall at 0.1 false alarms per minute remains 0.154 on CaptainCook4D and 0.034 on HoloAssist. No construction field trial.

selection_assessment.if_exactly_ten_required: Move EgoExoLearn to the first reading-path step and keep its comparative-label lesson there. Retain Ego-Exo4D as the main skill-data foundation, then add PROVIA for a distinct evaluation role. This is a scope tradeoff, not a criticism of EgoExoLearn’s evidence.
selection_assessment.flora: Keeping FLORA as a secondary practical annotation candidate is reasonable in the global shortlist. Its released segmentation/caption/reward inference is concrete, but the 40-episode dense test, failure recall and false positives limit confidence. It complements human review rather than replacing SkillSpotter or PROVIA.
selection_assessment.quality_comparison: SkillSpotter is for choosing moments for expert review. FLORA is for producing candidate event/quality labels. PROVIA is for assessing alarm behavior throughout executions. The report should preserve these distinct roles instead of combining their metrics.
selection_assessment.other_alternatives: FPL supports later multidimensional rubrics, PRISM supports transparent offline controls, and EGOSTREAM supports memory-validity diagnostics. None needs to replace the selected worker-memory core.

spotlight_review.product_path_assessment: The proposed pipeline is clearly marked as interpretation rather than a reproduced result. Separate event/availability times, evidence versus inferred state, held-out workers/sites and full cost accounting are appropriate. SuperMemory-VQA contributes an abstention design idea, not established calibrated open-ended uncertainty. No additional unsupported product claim found.
spotlight_review.limits: This is a source/card consistency cross-review. It does not independently reproduce all ten systems, validate released benchmark annotations or replace other agents’ pending final-source checks.

changes_verified: PROVIA now explicitly identifies 0.1 false alarms/minute as the validation budget. Recalls and dataset labels agree with exact Table IV, without claiming an actual test rate of 0.1.
MERIT still correctly describes final answering from retrieved frames.
MA-EgoQA reporting defects remain limited to the paper’s illustrated examples.
Eleven spotlight entries and the ProactEgoMem reading step retain the previously verified roles and limitations.
final_recheck.resolution: All factual clarification requests from this review are resolved. No further report-tail correction is required.

resolved.resolution: Now states final answering from retrieved frames, correctly separating text-only retrieval decisions from visual final QA.
Now explicitly limits the reporting inconsistency to the paper’s illustrated examples.
Eleventh row adds complete executions, recoveries, timing controls and false alarms. Selection balance is appropriate.

new_reading_step_check.result: Supported by current card and fresh memory-agent final receipt. Capturing and closing events, short clips and the oracle-performance gap are the relevant lessons. The draft does not imply continuous shift operation or measured wearable latency.

findings.observed_issue: The new row says recall “at 0.1 false alarms/minute”. The source uses a validation budget, with the resulting test false-alarm rates differing from 0.1. This shorthand also appeared in my proposed row and should be made exact.
findings.source_evidence: Exact PROVIA Table IV caption: thresholds are frozen on validation. At the 0.1 validation budget, actual test FA rates are 0.075 for CaptainCook4D and 0.093 for HoloAssist. Recalls 0.154 and 0.034 are correct.
findings.minimal_correction: Use “At a validation budget of 0.1 false alarms/minute, recall is 0.154 on CaptainCook4D and 0.034 on HoloAssist.”

full_review.limits: Source fidelity is not experimental reproduction, independent validation of published results, or human approval. The22 PDF-only records received metadata/inventory checks, not full methods review. Two deferred candidates remain abstract/metadata-only, and one deferred author full text lacks original PDF visuals. External access limitations are recorded separately.

spotlight.focus: Workers cameras, durable memory and execution quality

works.name: IndEgo
works.reason: Closest dataset to our work setting: mobile industrial tasks, collaborating wearers, task graphs and mistake annotations. A better starting point for industrial evaluation than household QA alone.
works.limit: Twenty participants in constrained workshops, partly staged errors, supplied segment boundaries and weak exact-match annotation agreement.

works.name: Ego-Exo4D
works.reason: Foundational skilled-activity recordings with synchronized viewpoints and expert feedback. Defines useful observations and annotation formats before choosing a model.
works.limit: Its skill labels mix several proxies. Aggregate recording hours and expert feedback do not establish construction-worker competence.

works.name: EgoExoLearn
works.reason: Makes relative skill assessment concrete through 34,239 retained comparisons and asynchronous demonstrations. Its controls show that an expert reference alone need not improve ranking.
works.limit: Cooking-centered comparisons, inconsistent reference gains and no verified worker-disjoint construction generalization.

works.name: AMEGO
works.reason: Inspectable interaction memory: persistent object tracks, visual features, times and locations. Complements caption retrieval with a concrete visual record of manipulated objects.
works.limit: Repeated similar objects and hand-interaction assumptions remain difficult. This is not validated defect detection or cheap all-day operation.

works.name: MERIT
works.reason: First practical retrieval baseline to evaluate: timestamped clips, several searchable keys, neighboring context and final answering from retrieved frames. Its simple episode design provides a useful control before adding WorldMM-style graphs.
works.limit: Large solver dependency, 0.56 reported retrieval hit rate, a 500-question EgoLifeQA test and initial captioning excluded from construction accounting.

works.name: MA-EgoQA
works.reason: Directly asks whether an answer requires evidence distributed across wearers. A useful design and evaluation reference for shared team memory, beyond independent personal archives.
works.limit: One household, generated questions, moderate performance and omitted memory-preparation cost. The paper’s illustrated examples contain reporting inconsistencies.

works.name: S-EMBER
works.reason: Makes the evidence interval part of success. Strong choice for testing whether a plausible answer can be traced back to the right video moment.
works.limit: Clips are 5–20 minutes. Multi-day memory is untested, two-pass selection uses 64+128 frames, and dataset access has restrictions.

works.name: EgoMemReason
works.reason: Multi-day questions require several evidence segments. Oracle-evidence controls help distinguish retrieval failure from reasoning failure, complementing S-EMBER's localization test.
works.limit: Five hundred questions from the same six people and environment, unequal model budgets, and a released option-mapping revision.

works.name: AEM
works.reason: Represents action effects as well as action identity. The most useful quality-model hypothesis here is to test what changed in the object, with task-specific correct executions as supervision.
works.limit: Offline cooking evaluation and supervised segmentation. EgoPER AUC changes from 73.8 to 86.7 with oracle segments. It does not uniformly outperform AMNAR.

works.name: SkillSpotter
works.reason: Separates finding a feedback-worthy moment from grading it. A concrete starting point for selecting clips for human review instead of producing an unexplained overall skill score.
works.limit: Subtle cooking/music events remain weak, pose and offline context are required, and matched-detection grading hides missed moments.

works.name: PROVIA
works.reason: Evaluates complete executions, recoveries and false alarms, with timing-only controls. A useful protocol for assessing whether quality alerts remain trustworthy throughout a task.
works.limit: Supervised segmentation/status training and simplified baselines. At a validation budget of 0.1 false alarms/minute, recall is 0.154 on CaptainCook4D and 0.034 on HoloAssist. No construction field trial.

spotlight.selection_scope: Entire final74-note corpus, not only this intake. Product-role shortlist rather than a cross-benchmark numerical ranking. Includes independently reviewed reading path and product interpretations.

candidate_reviews.problem_and_novelty: EgoLife extends egocentric benchmarks from short independent activities to a synchronized week in one shared household. EgoLifeQA asks personal memory questions across hours and days. EgoButler combines an audio-visual captioner with retrieval over caption memories, but the original QA benchmark does not require distributed evidence from multiple wearers.

architecture.input: Six wearers over seven days, with 15 synchronized external cameras and auxiliary sensors collected. The baseline answers questions about one wearer using audio-video clips.
architecture.components_and_flow: EgoGPT adds a Whisper audio branch to LLaVA-OneVision and generates captions for 30-second clips. EgoRAG stores descriptions and timestamps, conceptually summarizes them hourly/daily, retrieves relevant context and asks an evidence reader to answer. The reported implementation retrieves three clips by text similarity and uses GPT-4o for final answers in Table 5.
architecture.stored_representation: Persistent timestamped clip descriptions and proposed hourly/daily summaries. The implementation is a simple single-pass retrieval baseline rather than a demonstrated robust hierarchy with iterative correction.
architecture.output: A multiple-choice personal-memory answer. No calibrated execution-quality score.
architecture.training: EgoIT-99K supervised egocentric QA training, audio projection on LibriSpeech, and optional first-day EgoLife captions for identity adaptation.
architecture.streaming_and_causality: Architecture is described as continuously ingesting clips, but evaluation is offline on stored recordings. Past evidence constraints do not by themselves verify causal memory updates or exclusion of later summaries.
architecture.multi_wearer_vs_multiview: The dataset truly contains synchronized multiple wearers and fixed external views. EgoLifeQA and the reported Jake evaluation are single-wearer memory tasks, unlike MA-EgoQA.

results.claim: Personalization modestly improves the reported memory baseline.
results.value_and_protocol: Table 5 reports 36.0% average category accuracy for EgoGPT with first-day adaptation, versus 33.1% without and 36.9% with a Gemini-1.5-Pro captioner. The paper evaluates Jake’s 500 questions, not the full 3,000-question collection.
results.baseline: All Table 5 variants use the same EgoRAG framework and GPT-4o final answering. Chance is 25%.

results.claim: High-quality captions expose a significant bottleneck.
results.value_and_protocol: Human-verified visual-audio captions achieve 45.5 in Table 7 versus 36.0 for personalized generated audio-visual captions. Table 7 explicitly uses personalized EgoGPT for response generation, unlike Table 5’s GPT-4o final answer model.
results.baseline: Narrations alone score 31.5 and transcripts 29.6. These are input-representation ablations, not a full human QA ceiling.

results.claim: Retrieval helps when evidence lies beyond a short direct context.
results.value_and_protocol: For certificate lengths above 24 hours, EgoGPT plus EgoRAG scores 35.4 versus EgoGPT 25.0 and Gemini 18.4. Direct baselines receive only a half-hour segment.
results.baseline: Different evidence availability means this demonstrates the value of long-range retrieval, not superiority under equal full-video access.

reasons: Distinct long-duration collection with detailed multimodal annotations and explicit human QA refinement.
Baseline results remain close to chance, cover one participant, and report no uncertainty estimates.
The paper openly documents identity overfitting, missing audio understanding and retrieval failures.
quality.ablations_and_controls: Audio/visual modalities, first-day personalization, caption provenance, direct-context versus retrieved evidence. No ablation establishes that multiple wearer streams are necessary for original EgoLifeQA.
