The isolated routing gain is modest and does not imply faster inference.

architecture.input: Complete video before queries, without subtitles for Video-MME.
architecture.components_and_flow: TransNetV2 shot boundaries with 60-second minimum event merging create story profiles. Independent 30-second clips create fine logs at 1 fps. A reasoner sees the entire event storyline, localizes unexplored events and expands their cached clip text. A router can add up to eight frames per event to a 16-frame FIFO, with at most five reasoning iterations.
architecture.stored_representation: Two timestamped text caches plus query-local image FIFO. No explicit persistent physical-instance identity or spatial map.
architecture.output: An answer and supporting time periods, with a forced best-answer fallback after the iteration limit.
architecture.training: Frozen prompted Qwen3-VL-8B captioner and 32B reasoner. No task-specific training or learned router.
architecture.streaming_and_causality: Offline full-video indexing. This is not a causal continuous-stream evaluation, and the full event storyline grows with the video.
architecture.multi_wearer_vs_multiview: No multi-worker identity fusion or synchronized multi-view reconstruction.

results.value_and_protocol: Video-MME 2,700 questions: routed 67.5% and 5.76 online frames/query versus always-frames 67.2% and 6.63. No-frame version 65.3%.
results.baseline: Same pipeline with no frames or always-on frames, Table 9.

results.value_and_protocol: InfiniBench Global Appearance falls 62.80 to 58.90 and Character Actions 65.90 to 56.20 with routing, while Chronological Understanding improves 51.70 to 55.10.
results.baseline: Same pipeline without the router.

results.claim: Server-side cost is measured separately by stage
results.value_and_protocol: Two H200 GPUs, fixed eight-worker setup. Average captioner serving 222.1 s/video and reasoning 68.0 s/query. End-to-end averages including preprocessing/cache/extraction/orchestration are 229.3 s/video and 68.2 s/query. GPU energy 10.23 Wh per video plus three questions.
results.baseline: Always-frames online serving is 63.3 s and no-frames 59.6 s, both faster than routed 68.0 s.

results.claim: Router reliability is an outcome-based diagnostic
results.value_and_protocol: Retrieves frames on 46.2% of questions, captures 127/133 frame-beneficial cases. On 1,876 decidable questions, 127 true positives, 585 false positives, six false negatives and 1,158 true negatives. This is not human annotation of whether visual evidence is necessary.
results.baseline: Paired no-frame and always-frame outcomes define the oracle.

reasons: Published paper with explicit controlled routing tests and honest latency tradeoffs.
Many headline frame savings arise from the whole sparse pipeline, not the isolated router.
Egocentric transfer, deployment and fine workmanship are not evaluated.
quality.ablations_and_controls: Tests event-only, all clips, hierarchical text, images, routing, captioner size, reasoner size, frame budget, iteration count and multiple model families. Stronger dense Qwen3-VL remains 75.9% versus CFD 67.5%.
quality.leakage_or_dataset_limits: All queried content is indexed offline. Video-MME, InfiniBench and LVBench cover general video and edited film/TV. The authors explicitly identify shot segmentation as unsuitable for continuous wearable footage. No uncertainty calibration or sustained workload evidence.
quality.reproducibility_and_release: Official author project and ACL publisher verify identity/acceptance. No code link found on the checked official project or paper. All prompts and algorithm are described, but implementation reproduction remains incomplete.
quality.cost_and_scale: Appendix E provides ingestion, query, cached text size and server GPU energy, so cost is not wholly unreported. Fixed eight-worker measurement must not be treated as single-request device latency. Online frame counts exclude offline perception and do not represent cumulative pixel processing across every answering call. The edge tier is a server/desktop GPU, not measured glasses hardware.

comparison_to_wiki.difference: Much simpler caption hierarchy and visual-access gate, without episodic PPR, semantic facts or entity SQL. Shows whether raw pixels help after text fails, rather than supplying durable physical identity.
CFD can revisit raw historical video after a question, but requires full-video preprocessing. OneStreamer writes causal caption context and discards historical visual features.

verified_research_relations.source_location: Sections 2.1-2.2, cached clip memory replaces its query-time recaptioning role

candidate_reviews.verdict_reason: Keep as an existing simple visual-budget routing pattern. Its measured tradeoffs are useful, but it is not a top worker-memory spotlight over egocentric and identity-focused methods.
candidate_reviews.spotlight_case: A supporting engineering reference for deciding when to retrieve pixels. The router trades fewer frames for slightly longer serving time and worse appearance-heavy task results. Continuous worker footage needs a different event segmenter.

sources.supports: Exact local paper v1
EMNLP 2026 publication
Official project, retrieved successfully with curl after web-tool access failure

potential_note_issues: Existing note accurately limits mobile hardware claims, but should include Appendix E measured ingestion/query times and server energy rather than leave the impression that only frame counts exist.
Add video-qa, since answering questions is the actual evaluated task.
Mention that always-frames is better on InfiniBench appearance and character actions, relevant to execution-quality use.

identity.title: Never Look Back: Understanding Persistence in 3D Object Memory from Egocentric Videos
identity.pdf_path: raw/2026-chaudhari-ledger.pdf

reading.scope: Read full main paper, Appendix A construction, B HD-EPIC protocols/ablations/development, C VQ3D metrics and shared harness, D causality/counting/cost, E stitched-scene experiments, G failure analysis and H answer-time accounting. Inspected Figure 4 and Table 3 visually.

visual_pages_checked.content: Component ablation heatmap, model dependence and UCS-Bench evidence-condition table
visual_pages_checked.render: Embedded review or temporary artifact identifier: renders/c23/page9.png (not a live wiki path)

gaps: No experiments or repository installation were run.

candidate_reviews.problem_and_novelty: Persistent records of both touched and untouched physical objects join 3D observations, stable-location segments and contextual descriptions. The main value is diagnostic: object admission, persistence, camera reference frames, instance fragmentation and scene transitions affect different questions. It complements AMEGO interaction tracklets and OSNOM spatial tracking, rather than establishing a universally superior memory.

architecture.input: Egocentric recording with calibrated poses when available, otherwise estimated camera poses and uncertain scale.
architecture.components_and_flow: Qwen3.5-9B discovers object vocabulary, YOLO-World or SAM 3 detects, WildDet3D lifts observations, chronological label/proximity association creates tracks, a SAM 3 mask-propagation pass consolidates fragments. Three displaced observations confirm a new rest segment. Selected segments receive descriptions and triangulation can refine positions. Question-specific retrieval renders records for a single LLM call.
architecture.stored_representation: Object labels, timestamped boxes and 3D positions, rest segments and descriptions, camera trajectory. Gaps are unknown rather than evidence that an object remained stationary. Different scenes are not registered into one metric frame.
architecture.output: Spatial multiple-choice answers or named-object 3D positions, normally without source frames at answer time.
architecture.training: Pretrained perception and prompted Qwen/GPT readers. No new trained model. HD-EPIC thresholds and synonyms developed on separate calibration videos.
architecture.streaming_and_causality: Offline vocabulary discovery, reconstruction, consolidation and segmentation use the whole recording. Timestamp-filtered UCS-Bench answers are explicitly not a validated causal stream. Appending future footage may change prior memory states.
architecture.multi_wearer_vs_multiview: Multi-view triangulation is repeated viewpoints of a resting object. Stitched recordings can change wearer and camera but do not establish multi-worker synchronized identity fusion.

results.claim: Object memory improves blind answering on calibrated HD-EPIC
results.value_and_protocol: All 2,400 selected 3D Perception/Object Motion questions, prototype-averaged: GPT-5.4 blind 29.7%, LEDGER 42.6%, adapted AMEGO 34.7%. Published frame models use different answerers and protocols.
results.baseline: Released baseline memories rebuilt on the same frames and read with GPT-5.4.

results.claim: Memory is useful but does not replace frames
results.value_and_protocol: UCS-Bench 2,771 timestamped questions: blind 33.8, memory 38.5, 48 frames 44.4, frames plus LEDGER 46.3, frames plus routed DirectMe 42.9.
results.baseline: Matched evidence conditions.

results.claim: Sub-metre median localization is conditional on returned predictions
results.value_and_protocol: VQ3D SAM 3 trajectory memory with EgoLoc poses: median 0.99 m on 153/164 returned queries. On the shared 138-query subset, median 1.00 m versus adapted OSNOM 1.33 m.
results.baseline: Object-name retrieval with matched GPT-5.4 selection. Not the original crop-query VQ3D protocol.

results.value_and_protocol: Only 21/167 HourVideo recordings built. Tracking cost for dense recordings reached 74-3,500 hours per recording. On those 21, 358 questions: memory 41.1, frames 53.1, frames plus memory 49.4, latter decline not significant overall.
results.baseline: The completed subset is selected by construction tractability.

results.claim: Answer tokens are small but exclude ingestion
results.value_and_protocol: UCS-Bench 2,772-question accounting set: 2,044 input tokens memory versus 9,615 frames and 10,529 frames plus memory. HD-EPIC single-shot 1,750 tokens versus 22,850 for the same memory read agentically.
results.baseline: One extra question versus main Table 3 is documented.

reasons: Extensive matched-reader, shared-query and component analyses with paired tests and reported negative results.
Explicitly distinguishes offline construction, scale uncertainty and conditional localization metrics.
Very fresh preprint, severe construction cost and no real worker deployment.
quality.ablations_and_controls: Descriptions, persistence, triangulation, reader choice, pose source, detector, counting rules and scene boundaries are examined. Persistence ablation also changes inherited descriptions, so it is not a text-fixed isolation. Statistical correction and answering-run variability are disclosed.
quality.leakage_or_dataset_limits: Full-recording preprocessing is noncausal even after timestamp filtering. HD-EPIC calibrated poses and VQ3D scan-registered poses simplify geometry. Named-object queries and permissive custom success differ from official VQ3D. HourVideo has strong completion selection. The earlier ten-video pilot was used for development and explicitly excluded as held-out evidence.
quality.reproducibility_and_release: Actual public pipeline, reader and example memories exist. Repository calls itself a minimal working example. Only pose-free FastVGGT construction is released, examples with dataset-provided poses are included, and the complete evaluated harness is not claimed. Gated SAM 3 and dataset licenses are external requirements. README prompt-count claims use smaller sets than current paper, so do not assume exact full-paper reproduction.
quality.cost_and_scale: Single-shot query tokens are low but do not count local perception. WildDet3D component time about 0.85-0.99 s/detection on 24 GB GPU and dense-video tracking can be prohibitive. No reliable end-to-end streaming throughput established.

comparison_to_wiki.difference: Admits untouched fixtures and explicit coordinates, but AMEGO interaction tracklets outperform on some interaction/rest questions. Neither offers reliable object counts across clutter.
Adds object vocabulary and contextual records for language QA. Adapted OSNOM uses LEDGER detections/depth, so results are not a direct reproduction of the original complete OSNOM benchmark.

Both retain physical-instance history. LEDGER uses metric-or-unscaled geometry and stable-location segments, GEB uses visual appearance biographies and graph retrieval. GEB does not supply equivalent metric localization evidence.

candidate_reviews.verdict_reason: Retain for physical object history and valuable failure analysis. Strong relevance as a representation study, weaker readiness as an affordable worker-video backend.
candidate_reviews.spotlight_case: A focused representation spotlight for where tools were observed and how location records change. Pair it with its explicit noncausal construction, identity fragmentation, unknown intervals and 21/167 HourVideo completion limit. Do not pitch it as a scalable deployed pipeline.

sources.supports: Exact local v1 full paper
Official project and definition of LEDGER
Actual minimal code release and completeness limits

potential_note_issues: Current note is appropriately cautious. Quantify the construction-cost failure when considering practical component selection.
Do not describe 0.99 m as official end-to-end VQ3D performance or omit 153/164 coverage.
Keep frames-alone superiority and the confounded persistence ablation visible in detailed review.

identity.title: AMEGO: Active Memory from long EGOcentric videos
identity.pdf_path: raw/2024-goletto-amego.pdf

reading.scope: Read main paper including construction, baselines and component evaluation, Appendix 8 benchmark construction, 9 template-specific query logic, 10 threshold ablations and 11 pseudocode. Inspected Table 3 and Figure 5.

visual_pages_checked.content: AMB per-template results and performance versus duration
visual_pages_checked.render: Embedded review or temporary artifact identifier: renders/c24/page13.png (not a live wiki path)

gaps: No experiments or repository installation were run.

candidate_reviews.problem_and_novelty: An early reusable egocentric memory explicitly represents manipulated object instances, hand side and activity locations, rather than uniformly sampled embeddings or textual summaries. This is a distinct non-LLM foundation for temporal interaction queries. It does not attempt broad natural-language dialogue, metric 3D mapping or untouched-object persistence.

architecture.input: Untrimmed egocentric video, visual object/location query patches and one of eight query templates.
architecture.components_and_flow: Consistent class-agnostic hand-object detections initialize tracklets. EgoSTARK extends them beyond temporary hand disappearance, with hand visibility and new interactions controlling termination. Finished tracklets are represented with mean DINOv2 features and clustered online. Low optical flow and hand presence segment activity hotspots, which are clustered with SWAG features. Template-specific joins and temporal comparisons answer visual multiple-choice questions.
architecture.stored_representation: Interaction start/end, boxes, hand side, object cluster and appearance features, plus appearance-based location intervals. No metric coordinates or explicit object state changes.
architecture.output: Visual multiple-choice sequencing, concurrency and temporal-grounding answers. Ties or absent matches use random answer selection.
architecture.training: No additional model training. Uses pretrained HOI detector, EgoSTARK, DINOv2, SWAG and FlowFormer. Thresholds selected using two manually annotated videos.
architecture.streaming_and_causality: Memory construction is incremental and commits completed tracklets/segments. Benchmark queries run after processing the whole video, including before/after questions. This is not a measured live-response system.
architecture.multi_wearer_vs_multiview: One wearer per recording, no multi-worker identity transfer. Location clusters encode recurring visual hotspots, not multi-view geometry.

results.claim: Structured memory helps fine interaction questions
results.value_and_protocol: AMB approximately 20,500 questions from 100 EPIC-KITCHENS videos, five choices: AMEGO-L 36.3%, AMEGO-S 33.8%, strongest listed BLIP-2 semantic QA 23.6%, random 20%.
results.baseline: CLIP feature matching, caption plus LLaMA-2-7B and LLoVi-style two-stage caption summaries, with 4,096-token context limits.

results.value_and_protocol: On two manually annotated videos with 67 objects and 22 location instances, HOI predicted-to-GT temporal IoU 0.20, GT-to-predicted IoU 0.41 and 210 excess segments. Locations 0.36, 0.50 and 44 excess segments.
results.baseline: No tracker, no hand termination, weak temporal filtering and location filters.

results.value_and_protocol: AMEGO-L Q5 object concurrency 27.6%, while strongest BLIP-2 semantic baseline is 27.5%. Q8 location grounding 48.9% versus 26.2% for CLIP baseline.
results.baseline: Per-template comparison, not uniform improvement in all reasoning types.

reasons: Published foundational representation with public implementation and benchmark.
Useful structured-versus-unstructured comparison and component ablations.
Absolute accuracy is low and detailed component validation is tiny.
quality.ablations_and_controls: Initialization, termination, tracking, hand and flow filters, clustering thresholds and IoU thresholds tested. Component thresholds are optimized on the same two videos used for standalone component analysis, while one EPIC video is explicitly outside AMB.
quality.leakage_or_dataset_limits: AMB selects 100 recordings with VISOR masks and EPIC Fields poses, with mean duration 14 minutes. Ground-truth construction filters cases with repeated different instances of the same class in a video. Visual query crops are selected to minimize occlusion. This weakens evidence for difficult tool-instance discrimination in clutter. Historical baselines use small 2024-era LLMs and short context, not current memory agents.
quality.reproducibility_and_release: Actual HOI_AMEGO.py, LS_AMEGO.py, preprocessing tools, configuration, AMB and querying scripts are public. The environment and external detector/tracker/flow weights are documented but were not installed or executed.
quality.cost_and_scale: The reuse argument is architectural. No quantitative end-to-end ingestion throughput, query latency or storage savings are reported. Avoid efficient-processing solely because the memory is reusable.

comparison_to_wiki.difference: AMEGO captures contact and object-use intervals without geometry. LEDGER broadens coverage to untouched fixtures and records 3D rest segments, but AMEGO can remain better on interaction questions.
comparison_to_wiki.source_location: AMEGO Section 3 and LEDGER Table 2/Appendix B.4

comparison_to_wiki.difference: Both preserve appearance-linked instances. GEB observes broad object histories, adds graph retrieval and language biographies, whereas AMEGO gates memory on manipulation and uses simple template logic.

research_groups.paper_specific_evidence: Tushar Nagarajan is explicitly affiliated with FAIR, Meta on paper and official project.
Dima Damen at Bristol and explicit acknowledgement of the MaVi group on official project.

candidate_reviews.verdict_reason: Retain as a 2024 interaction-memory milestone and interpretable baseline. It adds a useful historical foundation beyond recent prompted graph agents.
candidate_reviews.spotlight_case: Good conceptual entry point for tool-use intervals and recurring work areas. Its low absolute accuracy, same-class instance filtering and lack of runtime evidence mean it is a baseline idea rather than a validated skill-assessment system.

sources.supports: Exact local v1 with appendix
Official ECCV project and affiliations
Actual implementation, benchmark and documented dependencies

potential_note_issues: Current note is accurate and already includes benchmark instance-filtering and runtime caveats.
Spatial-understanding means nonmetric activity hotspots here. Do not imply reconstructed scene coordinates.

identity.title: Beyond the Timeline: Augmenting Long-Video Memory with Grounded Entity Biographies
identity.pdf_path: Temporary screening artifact: c25.pdf (not a live wiki path)

reading.scope: Main §§1–5, Appendices A–D implementation/protocol/cost/controls and G limitations. Inspected actual ablation/evidence-coverage table and current release.
visual_pages_checked: Embedded review or temporary artifact identifier: renders/c25/page9.png: equal-context controls, entity and biography ablations (not a live wiki path)
gaps: No experiments or repository installation were run.

candidate_reviews.problem_and_novelty: Extends event-based retrieval with visually grounded physical-instance biographies, explicitly rejecting same-name objects observed apart. Unlike AMEGO tracklet grouping, connects instance encounters to richer episode/source context and lets a QA controller follow unsearched appearances. Unlike text-derived graphs, physical identity uses appearance and separation evidence.

architecture.input: Egocentric or other long video with captions/transcripts; raw frames for detection and grounding.
architecture.components_and_flow: YOLOE detections at10fps, BoT-SORT within30s clips, CLIP/DINO regrouping, Qwen3.5-35B descriptions from crops plus context. Sequential multimodal association requires a strong match, consistency with recent references and no same-frame separation. Entity–observation–episode–clip graph enables PPR retrieval and biography reading.
architecture.stored_representation: 308,244 observations,77,716 inferred entities for52h A1 week; graph has349,538 nodes and911,628 edges. Biographies preserve timestamps, crops, source/context links and unsearched-appearance references.
architecture.output: QA and temporal evidence via5-round controller,16units/round at week scale,64frame cap.
architecture.training: No model training. Thresholds visually calibrated per recording, prompted VLM descriptions and named-person profile consolidation.
architecture.streaming_and_causality: Offline memory written once. Queries re-index nodes before timestamp, but descriptions see ±40s context and person naming consolidates whole-day/across-day profiles. Node filtering alone does not prove construction-time causality.
architecture.multi_wearer_vs_multiview: Main week uses only participantA1. Persistent people are handled, but no joint multi-wearer sensor fusion.

results.value_and_protocol: 72.0% on500 EgoLifeQA and71.3% on50 A1 Ego-R1 questions (three seeds for latter).
results.baseline: MAGIC-Video67.6/64.7 with matched controller, answer model and retrieval limits. These baseline numbers are borrowed from its paper.

results.value_and_protocol: Full72.0%, noassociation68.6%, name-keyed69.2%, descriptions appended68.2%, no biography text68.0%.
results.baseline: Same backbone and bounded context controls.

results.value_and_protocol: EgoLife evidence hit58.9 vs37.6 on484 annotated questions. MultiHop completecoverage52.1 vs35.4%, answer score3.11vs2.58, but whole-clip Qwen3.5 scores3.64.
results.baseline: MAGIC-Video; score uses724 reference-answer questions, coverage1080; WorldMM52.6%coverage with more retrieved duration.

results.value_and_protocol: 5.6s/search and13.6s/question on50 Ego-R1 questions replayed against whole-week graph onA100.
results.baseline: Excludes controller, answering and ingestion. No measured end-to-end comparison.

reasons: Detailed matched-payload ablations and uncertainty make instance grounding credible.
New preprint with no implementation released.
Manual per-recording threshold calibration and future-context construction weaken live/automatic claims.
quality.ablations_and_controls: Independent association, name-keying, same-instance edges, context links, reading text, future-search references and increased baseline retrieval allowances. WorldMM achieves similar temporal coverage, so coverage alone does not establish better identities.
quality.leakage_or_dataset_limits: Three long egocentric evaluation variants share one A1 week. Day gameplay gain versusReMA is0.83points with CI includingzero. No direct human-annotated identity-association precision/recall. ±40s description context and across-day identity names raise a specific causal audit question.
quality.reproducibility_and_release: Official repository contains README/assets only and explicitly says code/artifacts coming soon. Not a ready component.
quality.cost_and_scale: 308k VLM descriptions plus10fps detection for52h creates substantial unmeasured ingestion work. Graph much larger than baselines. Retrieval latency excludes controller/answer generation and raw preprocessing.

comparison_to_wiki.difference: Retains AMEGO-like cross-time instance linkage but adds contextual biographies, visual contradiction checks and controlled language-QA/evidence studies.
Language-extracted entity relations versus explicit physical-instance association. Relevant to distinguishing two identical tools/materials.
GEB does not validate3D object persistence/hidden-state belief. Both motivate durable identities, but GEB is language-QA memory with offline identity estimates.

candidate_reviews.verdict_reason: A distinct, directly useful physical-identity lesson beyond current text graphs. Include as a carefully qualified preprint, not a production-ready or proven-online component.
candidate_reviews.spotlight_case: Conceptual spotlight for tracing the same tool/material through work episodes. Strongest contribution is controlled identity/biography ablation, while code absence, ingestion cost and causal-context concerns must be prominent.

sources.supports: Paper identity/version and full evaluation
Official repository release still pending

open_questions: Does query-time filtering also remove future context embedded in precomputed descriptions/person naming?
What are independently annotated instance association error rates?
When code appears, can ingestion be reduced below one VLM description per tracked observation?

identity.title: EgoMemReason: A Memory-Driven Reasoning Benchmark for Long-Horizon Egocentric Video Understanding
identity.pdf_path: Temporary screening artifact: c26.pdf (not a live wiki path)

reading.scope: Main §§1–5 and data construction, implementation, robustness and limitations appendices A–D. Main result Table 1 visually inspected on page 8.
gaps: No dataset execution or independent annotation audit.

candidate_reviews.problem_and_novelty: Requires accumulating entity, event and behavior evidence across days rather than locating one memorable moment. Distinct from MA-EgoQA multi-wearer fusion and ordinary EgoLife QA.

architecture.input: EgoLife recordings before a question timestamp
architecture.components_and_flow: Object-centric 30s captions and hierarchical summaries generate questions, then blind-LLM filtering, visual evidence checks and two-tier human verification produce six task types.
architecture.stored_representation: A benchmark with evidence references, not a new deployed memory store.
architecture.output: Multiple-choice answer for entity tracking/counting, event ordering/linking, or behavior inference.
architecture.training: Evaluates existing VLMs and agents.
architecture.streaming_and_causality: Query-time causal prefix constraint, but sampled-frame or retrieval evaluation is not bounded-state streaming.
architecture.multi_wearer_vs_multiview: Built from six EgoLife participants, questions mainly use one participant history rather than mandated cross-wearer fusion.

results.value_and_protocol: 500 questions, average 5.1 evidence segments and 25.9 hours backtracking. Best overall 39.6% Gemini-3-Flash, WorldMM 30.6%, random 16.8%.
results.baseline: 17 systems with heterogeneous frame limits and agent settings

results.value_and_protocol: Gemini-3-Flash improves from 39.6% to 67.2% when given oracle evidence.
results.baseline: Full-video setting

reasons: Explicit causal evidence constraints and human second-tier full-recording audit.
Oracle evidence, query-only, frame-scaling and filtering robustness analyses help diagnose failures.
Published acceptance independently confirmed in COLM proceedings.
quality.ablations_and_controls: Temporal certification, frame count, captions/transcripts, CoT/ICL, query-only and oracle evidence.
quality.leakage_or_dataset_limits: Only six participants and one living environment. Generation/filtering uses evaluated model families. Tier-1 annotators see proposed label, mitigated by independent tier-2 re-answering. Main text 1024-frame description differs from appendix best-budget selection, so ranking is not compute-matched.
quality.reproducibility_and_release: Official repo, annotations and leaderboard exist. Dataset v1.1 reshuffles option letters, requiring prediction remapping. Raw EgoLife access is separate.
quality.cost_and_scale: Caption preparation at 1FPS per 30s clip for agents, but end-to-end ingestion and retrieval costs are not a central controlled result.

comparison_to_wiki.difference: Reuses recordings but adds evidence aggregation across multiple days and entity/event/behavior diagnostics.
Evaluated baseline with 30.6% overall, illustrating the limits of episodic/semantic/visual memory on this harder question set.
Long-range within-history reasoning rather than shared cross-wearer context.

candidate_reviews.verdict_reason: Adds a complementary multi-day evidence-aggregation stress test, with unusually useful oracle and human-validation diagnostics.
candidate_reviews.spotlight_case: Strong candidate for designing multi-day worker-memory tests. Use alongside grounded short-horizon retrieval, not as proof of construction transfer or general skill measurement.

sources.supports: Exact full paper
Independent venue confirmation
Code and benchmark version notice
500-row annotation release and license

open_questions: Verify exact per-model frame budgets before using rankings quantitatively.
Test generalization beyond six housemates.
Avoid inferring the UNC lab from coauthor reputation alone.

identity.title: EgoProbe: Benchmarking Long-Range and Exact Memory in Streaming Egocentric Videos
identity.pdf_path: Temporary screening artifact: c27.pdf (not a live wiki path)

reading.scope: Main sections 1–5, Appendix B.3–B.6, C–E, supporting tables and protocol details.
gaps: No public release located. Appendix B.1–B.2 and prompts not exhaustively audited.

candidate_reviews.problem_and_novelty: Separates distant retention from confusing one repeated event with another. Unlike generic long-context QA, Echo distractors are actual details from other events and a second dialogue turn asks the target-specific detail. Base and Echo are not matched causal controls.

architecture.input: Ego4D/QaEgo4D and EgoLife video prefixes. 2,366 independent QA pairs across 671 videos, with 1,229 derived two-turn dialogues.
architecture.components_and_flow: Discover related events using descriptions, delay query, disambiguate reference, create event-grounded distractors, then human verify clips and relevant history. Evaluate 19 model configurations.
architecture.stored_representation: Benchmark metadata stores event timestamps, option-to-event links, query times and target detail. Baseline memory types vary.
architecture.output: Four-option single-turn answer and yes/no then four-option two-turn answer.
architecture.training: No new model training contribution.
architecture.streaming_and_causality: Strict streaming models cannot reload discarded video and do not see future queries. Offline references retain query-time access to video prefix. Query answers branch from memory without contaminating persistent state.
architecture.multi_wearer_vs_multiview: Single-stream recall tasks using source datasets, not fused multiple-worker reasoning.

results.value_and_protocol: StreamForest Base 50.66%, Echo single-turn 38.89%, two-turn completion 35.39%. R2 denominator is all 1,229 dialogues and requires both turns correct.
results.baseline: GPT-5.6-Sol prefix reference Base 55.32%, completion 43.69%, with different input/history-access budget.

results.value_and_protocol: StreamForest event-linked errors 38.04% with one related event and 61.64% with at least three. Different groups are not matched examples.
results.baseline: Random event-linked error references 25% and 53.01%, respectively.

results.value_and_protocol: Qwen3.5 text-only 25.51% Base and 24.49% Echo, versus 45.91% and 35.31% with video.
results.baseline: 25% chance for four options.

reasons: Directly valuable diagnostic for repeated physical work.
Explicit strict-streaming harness and honest distinction from prefix processing.
Fresh preprint with code/data promised rather than inspectable.
All R1 labels affirmative, so coarse recall score is confounded by yes-response bias.
quality.ablations_and_controls: Text-only reference, recall bins, event-linked distractor counts and two-turn decomposition. No matched intervention that isolates distractor interference from other subset differences.
quality.leakage_or_dataset_limits: Annotators see original labels, no inter-annotator agreement reported. 24.4% of questions need at least 30-minute recall, only 113 ultra-long independent items. Gemini construction roles, sparse source families and all-positive R1.
quality.reproducibility_and_release: Paper says code and data will be released. Search did not locate an official implementation or dataset as of 2026-10-31.
quality.cost_and_scale: 128 prefix frames for general models, 512 for VideoChat-Flash, heterogeneous memory/compute budgets. Maximum recall 138.54 hours includes recording gaps. No normalized latency/cost comparison.

comparison_to_wiki.difference: Controls event reference/distractor provenance and enforces strict streaming for a subset of baselines.
EgoProbe has distinctive event-grounded wrong answers. EgoMemReason targets compositional memory, EGOSTREAM validity windows, S-EMBER evidence localization.

candidate_reviews.verdict_reason: Distinct diagnostic of binding the correct detail to a repeated event is highly relevant to workers repeating the same operation. Add with unreleased-preprint caveat and do not rank models across unequal protocols.

architecture.components_and_flow: GPT-4 Turbo reads full future narrations to derive target goals, beliefs and actions. It generates counterfactual alternatives from prior context, then applies length and similarity filters, repeated no-context model screening and author visual review. Existing models answer zero-shot.
architecture.stored_representation: Benchmark questions, choices and source timestamps. No learned persistent memory.
architecture.output: Selected goal, belief or future action choice and cross-question consistency.
architecture.training: No new model trained. Generation and inference use existing LLMs and VLMs.
architecture.streaming_and_causality: Model inputs nominally end at the query moment, while label generation deliberately uses the future. Annotation timing sometimes exposes the start of the target future action in the final input frames.
architecture.multi_wearer_vs_multiview: One wearer at a time. Social interactions can occur but this is neither a multi-stream benchmark nor a cross-wearer memory method.

results.claim: Goals are easier than beliefs and next actions.
results.value_and_protocol: Figure 4 and pages 6–7 report roughly 90% human goal accuracy, 70% belief accuracy and 77% action accuracy, compared with model belief/action accuracy around 50% at best. These are rounded plot/prose values. Models were evaluated on 70% of the final 1,039-question benchmark while quality checks were still in progress. Four internal human participants answered a subset of 225 unique questions.
results.baseline: Chance is 1/3 for goals and 1/4 for beliefs/actions. Human and model aggregate test sets are not identical.

results.claim: Longer visual history does not reliably improve inference.
results.value_and_protocol: Uniform frame counts remain fixed as duration increases. VideoLLaMA2 with 16 frames does not consistently improve over its 8-frame variant. Humans also show little gain between 5 and 30 seconds of context on their small subset.
results.baseline: Text narration histories usually improve more with duration. Richer text context and sparse visual context are not equivalent information budgets.

reasons: The paper explicitly distinguishes inferred mental states from objectively observed futures and documents ambiguity.
Repeated choice shuffling and no-context filtering address specific benchmark shortcuts.
Evaluation was incomplete at publication and human comparison is small and internal.
quality.ablations_and_controls: Text versus video, model size, context duration, no-context controls and error/choice consistency. No worker skill or quality outcome evaluation.
quality.leakage_or_dataset_limits: Labels encode one plausible belief consistent with an eventual action, not actual private beliefs. Multiple alternatives can remain valid. Annotation timing can leak the next action. Generation filters use some evaluated model families.
quality.reproducibility_and_release: Official facebookresearch repository contains annotation directories, evaluation code and VLMEval configuration. Source Ego4D videos retain their own access conditions. Current primary sources identify the work as a 2025 preprint, with no conference acceptance verified.
quality.cost_and_scale: 785 source clips with 1,039 questions. Source clips are approximately 5 minutes, query moments fall between 2.5 and 4.5 minutes. This does not test day-scale memory.

comparison_to_wiki.difference: Derives first-order mental-state and action questions from its narrations rather than collecting a new camera network.
MA-EgoQA tests retrieving factual distributed observations across wearers. EgoToM tests single-person latent intent inferred from future behavior.
EgoTaskQA covers task structure and object-state causal traces. EgoToM adds naturalistic goal-conditioned counterfactual beliefs, but has weaker ground truth for actual beliefs.

research_groups.paper_specific_evidence: Five authors explicitly list Reality Labs on the first page.
Asli Celikyilmaz explicitly lists FAIR on the first page. Verify whether this identifier exists before ingestion.

candidate_reviews.verdict_reason: Defer for scope. The useful distinction between observed facts and inferred intent can be retained as context, but speculative beliefs are less directly useful for auditable worker memory and execution quality than EgoTaskQA, EgoExoLearn and evidence-grounded QA candidates.
candidate_reviews.spotlight_case: Do not spotlight. No persistent memory or task-quality measurement, and beliefs should never be presented as observed worker facts.
open_questions: Would human choice distributions be a better target than a single inferred belief?
Does the released benchmark now include evaluations of all questions rather than the 70% used in the paper?

candidate_reviews.problem_and_novelty: MM-Ego combines 7 million narration-derived egocentric QA training samples, the EgoMemoria benchmark, and a supervised memory pointer that selects detailed frame embeddings after a cheap global glimpse. architecture.input: One egocentric video, up to 300 uniformly sampled frames, and a question. Videos range from 30 seconds to 1 hour.
architecture.components_and_flow: SigLIP-so400m features pass through an MLP and spatial pooling. Each frame is also pooled to one token. Qwen2-7B reads these compressed tokens, the question and a learned pointer. Pointer-to-frame scores plus a uniform exploration bias select 32 frames. A second Qwen pass reads their detailed visual embeddings to answer.
architecture.stored_representation: Per-frame low-resolution and high-resolution embeddings within a video. No persistent cross-session database, identity memory or bounded-retention policy is proposed.

architecture.training: Initialize from LLaVA-OneVision 7B. One epoch of joint image/video SFT with 7 million generated egocentric QA samples and other multimodal datasets. Language loss trains answers, binary cross-entropy supervises pointer scores using narration-derived key frames. Training fallback receives ground-truth rather than predicted frames.
architecture.streaming_and_causality: Offline complete-video global glimpse and second pass. It is not an online update method. Always-on and hierarchical memory are listed as future work.
architecture.multi_wearer_vs_multiview: Single-wearer video reading. No coordinated cross-camera evidence.

results.claim: Both specialized training and the pointer improve EgoMemoria.
results.value_and_protocol: Table 3 mean debiased accuracy is 47.32 for LLaVA-OV, 55.97 for Ego SFT using the same data mixture, and 61.27 for MM-Ego. The marginal pointer gain over the matched SFT baseline is 5.30 percentage points, not 13.95 points. Original accuracy is 65.45, 76.30 and 79.56 respectively.
results.baseline: Matched 7B backbone and training mixture distinguish data gains from architecture gains. MDA averages three model-conditioned filtered test subsets and three duration groups, not raw overall question accuracy.

results.claim: Comparison with a closed model depends on metric and frame budget.

results.baseline: Unequal preprocessing budgets and specialized training prevent interpreting this as a universal better model.

results.claim: Fewer detailed frames preserve much of the score.
results.value_and_protocol: MM-Ego drops from 61.27 MDA with 32 selected frames to 58.46 with 4, a 4.59% relative drop. The global glimpse still requires the candidate frame representation.
results.baseline: Ego SFT drops 55.97 to 51.95, 7.19% relative. No wall-clock or GPU-memory benchmark is reported.

candidate_reviews.problem_and_novelty: MA-EgoQA turns the synchronized EgoLife recordings into explicit cross-wearer factual, temporal and social questions. architecture.input: Prepared caption memories from six EgoLife wearers over seven days, and a five-choice question. Optional retrieved video frames are tested separately.
architecture.components_and_flow: Every 10-minute window, a manager merges all agents’ captions into events with when, what, where, who and how. BM25 retrieves 20 shared records. An LLM turns the question and these records into agent-specific subqueries. Each retrieves five individual records, retaining scores at least 10. A final model answers using shared and individual evidence.
architecture.stored_representation: Individual caption stores plus centralized structured event records indexed by BM25. Video remains available for optional evidence reading.

architecture.streaming_and_causality: Windowed memory construction is described causally, but all experiments use stored recordings and prepared memories. No live ingestion test or end-to-end real-time guarantee.
architecture.multi_wearer_vs_multiview: True synchronized multiple wearers, not one ego camera plus fixed exo cameras. The claim that every question requires more than two agents is stronger than demonstrated: Figure 8 includes two-agent cases, and Appendix D examples list one or two source wearers.

results.claim: Shared retrieval improves the strongest matched caption baseline.
results.value_and_protocol: EgoMAS with Gemini 2.5 Flash achieves 41.41% on 1,741 questions versus 36.93% for all-caption concatenation with that backbone, a 4.48 percentage-point gain. Oracle generation context reaches 83.80%.
results.baseline: Five-choice chance is 20%. Oracle uses the context from question generation and is not a human ceiling. Adapted single-stream methods face restricted routing, so their scores should not be treated as universal inferiority.

results.claim: Both memory construction and dynamic retrieval contribute.
results.value_and_protocol: With Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct, accuracy is 27.80 without either module, 28.20 with dynamic retrieval only, 30.04 with shared memory only, and 35.55 with both. NV-Embed-v2 retrieval yields 37.91 versus BM25 35.55.
results.baseline: Shared-memory alternatives range from 25.96 for chunks to 31.99 for a graph. BM25 is a lighter baseline, not the most accurate retriever.

results.claim: Measured query latency is small after memories are prepared.
results.value_and_protocol: Reported mean latency is 1.3 seconds on 100 randomly selected questions using Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct. It excludes video captioning and memory construction.
results.baseline: The 41.41% headline uses a different, stronger backbone. Do not combine that accuracy with this latency into one operating point.

results.claim: More wearers help, but the evidence does not prove every question needs all views.
results.value_and_protocol: Appendix A.2 reports 31.99% with one available agent versus 35.55% with six. Adding frames to Qwen2.5 EgoMAS improves SI/TR/EI but reduces TC by 0.62 points and ToM by 1.28 points.
results.baseline: Single-agent filtering checks named people or one randomly chosen wearer when no name is present, not an exhaustive all-agent information-theoretic guarantee.
results.source_location: Figure S2, section 4.2 and Table S11.

reasons: Directly targets cross-wearer evidence aggregation and includes matched-backbone module ablations.

candidate_reviews.problem_and_novelty: Maps masonry quality-supervision requirements to worker-camera activity queries, then adopts an existing VSGN temporal action detector to retrieve intervals for human inspection. architecture.input: Recorded egocentric construction footage and a query from a predefined activity-category list.
architecture.components_and_flow: Pre-extracted SlowFast Kinetics-400 features feed the VSGN graph pyramid, scoring/localization heads and category-wise NMS. Query filters select relevant category proposals. Mapped supervision requirements help humans review retrieved clips.
architecture.stored_representation: Temporal action features/proposals with class, start/end and confidence. No durable semantic memory, language QA or state graph.
architecture.output: Intervals of queried activities. The system does not automatically judge quality deviations.
architecture.training: SlowFast features at 1.87 per second, 2304 dimensions. Five graph scales, 30 epochs, batch 32, learning rate .0001. A 6:2:2 split is described as disjoint video frames.
architecture.streaming_and_causality: Section 4.1 explicitly assumes the query comes at the end of the video. Section 7.3.2 explicitly says real-time quality-deviation detection is not supported. Real-time documentation language must not be interpreted as causal quality monitoring.
architecture.multi_wearer_vs_multiview: Section 7.3.3 explicitly says synchronized fusion of multiple workers’ videos is not implemented. Detecting interaction existence does not infer conversation content or individual quality responsibility.

results.claim: Temporal activity retrieval, not defect detection.
results.value_and_protocol: Average mAP 6.07% across tIoU .1,.2,.3,.4,.5 versus baseline 5.68%. At tIoU .5, 3.47% versus 3.57%, so the method is not better at every threshold.
results.baseline: Ego4D baseline cited as reference 20.

results.claim: Reported recall aggregate is permissive and protocol-specific.
results.value_and_protocol: Validation recall 35.85% versus 34.79%, averaged over Table 6 settings k=1–5 and tIoU=.3,.5,.7. x is the number of ground-truth instances of the queried category and the system can return top k*x proposals. False positives for absent categories are not penalized by this recall metric.
results.baseline: Ego4D baseline in Table 6.
results.source_location: Section 5.4, Table 6. Note prose lists k=1–3 while Table 6 has k=1–5.

reasons: Direct construction-camera relevance and useful explicit limitations.
The detector is largely adopted VSGN, with no clear component ablations or strong matched construction-specific baselines.

reading.scope: Main paper pp. 1–9 in full, appendix protocol, SRL construction, decoder controls, type-specific errors and paired bootstrap confidence intervals, especially F.5 and Tables 20–21. References checked for dataset and baseline relations.

candidate_reviews.problem_and_novelty: Post-completion procedural mistake recognition from step clips. PRISM separates language grounding, semantic representation, learned local emissions, sequence decoding and edit alignment, with unusually explicit controls for whether structured semantic-role text and sequence reasoning actually help. Its contribution is interpretable diagnosis and controlled analysis, not an end-to-end streaming quality inspector.

architecture.input: Complete videos with benchmark-provided temporal step boundaries, per-task candidate step descriptions and valid reference sequences.
architecture.components_and_flow: Gemini 3 Flash or Qwen3.5-27B describes each step clip. Raw text or GPT-5.3/Qwen3.6-generated predicate–argument SRL is embedded, projected by training-only PCA and decoded by a per-task HMM. Viterbi step IDs align to valid reference sequences, with semantic and anomaly checks for insertion, deletion, substitution and transposition.
architecture.stored_representation: Per-task step prototypes, smoothed transitions, Gaussian or cosine emissions, text/SRL embeddings and valid reference sequences.
architecture.output: Step-level error locations/types after completion. This is not defect severity, workmanship quality or physical safety certification.
architecture.training: Only correct executions fit the HMM. Validation chooses thresholds/configurations. EgoOops has only 21 correct training videos and no validation split, so configurations transfer from the other two benchmarks.
architecture.streaming_and_causality: Explicitly offline post-completion, with ground-truth step segmentation and complete sequence alignment. No bounded streaming or online alarm evidence.
architecture.multi_wearer_vs_multiview: Egocentric benchmark inputs, not multi-worker memory fusion.

results.claim: Structured semantic roles have small, conditional benefits under matched downstream settings.
results.value_and_protocol: Matched Raw→GPT-SRL Any-F1: Qwen EgoOops .321→.356, EgoPER .578→.601, CaptainCook4D .587→.592. Gemini .349→.353, .602→.631, .595→.596. Paired video bootstrap with 10,000 replicates excludes zero for only three of six gains.
results.baseline: Identical downstream configuration with raw descriptions.

results.claim: Local learned emissions are more consistently useful than sequence decoding.
results.value_and_protocol: Greedy learned emissions beat nearest-candidate matching in all 12 matched conditions. Viterbi improves seven, ties four and hurts one, including no change on EgoPER.
results.baseline: Nearest candidate and greedy emissions under matched conditions.

results.claim: Published system comparisons are protocol dependent.
results.value_and_protocol: CaptainCook4D Gemini+SRL EDA .843/AUC .900 versus AMNAR .723/.602 and AEM predicted-segment .719/.625. On EgoPER AEM with GT segments .747/.867 exceeds PRISM .713/.762. These are reported baseline scores with different segmentation/configuration protocols.
results.baseline: AMNAR and AEM from their papers, not a newly matched rerun.

reasons: Three datasets, explicit grounding versus privileged gold-text conditions, training-only correct executions and matched decoder controls.
Confidence intervals honestly show that half the matched SRL gains are uncertain.

candidate_reviews.problem_and_novelty: Goal-conditioned pairwise progress comparison with order-swapped diagnostic tests, LongTag subtask context and failure-aware supervision. The new emphasis beyond earlier EgoTSR is non-monotonic regression/recovery evaluation. It estimates which observed state is closer to a goal, not worker skill or construction defect quality.

architecture.input: Task instruction and two images from one execution. LongTag also receives an ordered subtask outline predicted from the initial image and task.
architecture.components_and_flow: Successful approximately monotonic trajectories provide pair labels, both input orders are generated, teacher reasoning supplies CoT supervision, and CoT→Tag full-parameter training teaches a Qwen2.5-VL-7B comparator. Failure-aware fine-tuning adds annotated regressions and recoveries.
architecture.stored_representation: Learned model parameters and separate subtask planner, not persistent episodic memory.
architecture.output: Binary preference over candidate task states. Qualitative aggregated curves do not establish calibrated completion percentages.
architecture.training: Robot trajectories from AgiBot/Open X-Embodiment and human EPIC/Ego4D data. Paper claims trajectory-level splitting before pair generation. CoT, direct labels and LongTag support curriculum training.
architecture.streaming_and_causality: Pairwise offline diagnostic. No continuous causal alarm system, persistent memory, closed-loop control or construction-site experiment.
architecture.multi_wearer_vs_multiview: Multiple datasets/viewpoint domains, not multi-worker memory fusion.

results.value_and_protocol: 87.5% short-horizon accuracy, macro average over eight window categories, and 92.4% long-horizon average with 0.1-point forward/inverse Gap.
results.baseline: Qwen2.5-VL-7B 55.6% short-horizon and 49.8% long-horizon.

results.claim: Failure-aware supervision improves recovery but reduces success-test accuracy.
results.value_and_protocol: On 1,345 physical pairs / 2,690 ordered items at Window 10, failure accuracy 64.1→75.9%, recovery 58.6→69.8%, regression error 32.8→23.4%. Success test drops 88.2→84.1%. Recovery/regression subsets cover only 9/24 source videos.

results.claim: LongTag structured context is beneficial under the reported matched ablation.
results.value_and_protocol: Long-horizon accuracy 81.1→92.4% and Gap 4.3→0.1 when subtask skeleton is supplied.
results.baseline: LongTag without subtask skeleton.

reasons: Useful matched input-order diagnostic and explicit failure-aware test distinguish chronology from task state.
No uncertainty estimates and small source-video support for recovery.
Important reproducibility details deferred to an absent supplement. The ++ implementation is not verified.

Table 6 single-image baseline has a 9.4-point Gap despite separately scoring each image. Under deterministic score comparison this would be invariant to swapping except ties or unstated randomness/protocol differences. This is an unresolved reporting concern, not proof of invalid results.

candidate_reviews.verdict_reason: Keep the existing accurately scoped note, with stronger reproducibility and reporting caveats. Not a high-confidence operational spotlight.

existing_note_findings.current_text: Temporal labels remain conditional on approximately monotonic success. Order invariance alone cannot establish physical correctness. These benchmarks do not validate construction defects, worker competence or downstream robot control. This note follows the main two-stage method, rather than treating the broader planning imagery in introductory Figure 1 as an evaluated deployment.

existing_note_findings.proposed_replacement: Temporal labels depend on approximately monotonic success. Order invariance alone cannot establish physical correctness. Recovery evaluation covers only nine source videos. The PDF refers to supplementary split and training details that are absent from this version, and a release for EgoTSR++ is unverified. Table 6 also reports a nonzero order gap for a separately scored single-image baseline, without explaining tie handling or other order-dependent effects. cross_reviews.selection_rationale: A well-targeted diagnostic for distinguishing the wearer and the wearer-associated objects from other people and visually similar objects. Human-authored questions and comparison of open-ended with multiple-choice answers add credible marginal value. It is especially relevant before building worker-specific memory, while its temporal horizon and oracle analysis sharply limit claims of durable memory.
corrected_or_qualified_claims: Main evaluation is causal to the question timestamp: uniform sampling uses only the video prefix, usually 32 frames and at most 1 fps. LongVA/LongVU receive 128 frames, so comparisons across those models are not frame-matched.

Table 3 is an oracle evidence-availability experiment. It uses known answer and question moments, eight frames within ±1.5 seconds around each. The paper does not clearly state whether the positive offset around the question is clipped. Do not present this as a deployable or proven causal retrieval gain.

The Table 3 uniform baseline differs slightly from Table 2 for several open models. Quote Table 3 pairs together rather than subtracting across tables. Gemini Previous is 40.3 to 51.5, while Qwen2.5 is 33.2 to 42.4.

Human 84.7 open-ended accuracy is from 300 questions answered by two university students, rather than the full 5,012-question model evaluation. The numerical full-table gap is therefore descriptive rather than a matched estimate.
Ninety percent of answer-to-query intervals are below 40 seconds. The nine-minute average source video does not imply that the questions test nine-minute or shift-long retention.

Prompt effects are small and mixed. Table 4 includes declines under the enhanced prompt and an improvement after removing personalization cues. Avoid a general claim that enhanced prompting reliably solves ego-grounding.

cross_reviews.selection_rationale: The benchmark has thoughtful automatic and author quality checks, including repeated shuffled no-context controls. Nevertheless, its target is inferred goals, beliefs and immediate next actions, with less direct current product value than grounded evidence retrieval and state/quality tracking. Labels encode plausible mental-state explanations inferred retrospectively from future behavior, not measured worker beliefs or competence. Defer on scope and construct validity, not because the benchmark has no merit.
corrected_or_qualified_claims: The paper reports results on 70% of the final questions while human filtering was still in progress. Human results use four internal participants over 225 unique questions. Do not call this a fully evaluated final benchmark with an external expert human study.
Goal inference has three choices and 33% chance, while belief/action have four choices and 25% chance. Their raw accuracies are not directly comparable task-difficulty measures.

Video conditions hold the sampled frame count fixed while varying context duration, often including the last frame. Longer context therefore changes temporal density rather than monotonically adding visual information. The paper explicitly acknowledges this on p. 7.
Narration-conditioned model results use privileged human descriptions. They should remain separate from video-only results.

Counterfactual alternatives are constructed conditional on the true goal. This makes the benchmark a constrained retrospective inference task and does not establish access to the wearer’s actual private beliefs.

cross_reviews.selection_rationale: A useful 2025 milestone for query-guided coarse-to-fine frame access: a cheap per-frame global representation chooses detailed frames for a second LLM pass, and a same-data fine-tuned baseline partly isolates the architectural gain. This adds a concrete retrieval architecture and a useful language-shortcut diagnostic, despite incomplete release and synthetic benchmark limits. Medium priority rather than a production-ready memory recommendation.
corrected_or_qualified_claims: The architectural increment on the paper’s MDA metric is 61.27 minus 55.97 = 5.30 points against Ego SFT. The 13.95-point difference from 47.32 includes both egocentric SFT data and the pointer architecture.

MDA averages accuracy over model-conditioned no-video filtered subsets and duration groups. It is a diagnostic average, not an unbiased population accuracy. Raw accuracy is separately 65.45, 76.30 and 79.56 for the base, Ego SFT and MM-Ego models.
MM-Ego searches up to 300 sampled frames in the global glimpse and then selects 32 detailed frames. GPT-4o receives only 32 uniformly sampled frames. This is not an equal visual-access comparison.

Table 5 reduces the number of detailed fallback frames. The compressed global glimpse and encoding cost remain, so the 32-to-4 result does not establish an eightfold end-to-end cost reduction or bounded online memory.
Training uses ground-truth key frame indices for detailed inputs, while inference uses selected indices. Keep this supervised oracle-to-predicted distinction visible.
The two-minute wearable example is a demonstration, not a field evaluation of worker quality or persistent memory. No released full implementation was verified in the original receipt.

changes.old: Later multiple-choice QA compares uniformly sampled frames, frames preserved through predicted tool calls, and oracle event windows. Thus, the benchmark measures both acquisition behavior and whether the resulting visual evidence supports answers. It does not assume captions are a sufficient memory representation (§5.4).
changes.new: Later multiple-choice QA compares no memory, predicted tool memory, and oracle memory. Information-capture QA uses trace text plus up to 40 frames from the selected intervals. State- and location-tracking QA use text-only tool traces containing object names, states or locations, and times. The no-memory control receives 40 uniformly sampled frames from the full clip (§5.4, Appendix K.3).

changes.old: Temporal labels remain conditional on approximately monotonic success. Order invariance alone cannot establish physical correctness. These benchmarks do not validate construction defects, worker competence or downstream robot control. This note follows the main two-stage method, rather than treating the broader planning imagery in introductory Figure 1 as an evaluated deployment.
changes.new: Temporal labels depend on approximately monotonic success. Order invariance alone cannot establish physical correctness. Recovery evaluation covers only nine source videos. The PDF refers to supplementary split and training details that are absent from this version, and a release for EgoTSR++ is unverified. Table 6 also reports a nonzero order gap for a separately scored single-image baseline, without explaining tie handling or other order-dependent effects. Construction defects, worker competence and downstream robot control remain unvalidated.

changes.old: Edge/cloud separation is simulated, with no mobile-hardware, network, or energy validation (Limitations).
changes.new: Appendix E reports GPU energy and average end-to-end costs of 229.3 seconds per video for indexing and 68.2 seconds per query in the fixed eight-worker setup on two H200 GPUs. Edge/cloud separation is simulated, without mobile-hardware or real-network validation (Limitations, Table 15).

changes.old: Memory is updated causally during streaming, although background construction still consumes computation.
changes.new: Memory is updated causally during streaming, although background construction still consumes computation. The evaluation pauses the video clock during reactive answers, so it does not establish uninterrupted live ingestion while answering (Appendix C.5).

sections.heading: Summary
sections.content:
# Wiki Audit — 2026-10-31

Historical snapshot: this report and its CSV describe the wiki before prompt consolidation, the conversion of the group register into profiles, the replacement of the mixed index with a table of existing notes, and the conversion of the search log into a stage log. Their original paths and counts are retained as audit evidence. These structural changes received targeted checks, not a new full content or external-link audit.

Added **30 notes**, bringing the wiki to **54 notes and 79 unchanged source PDFs**. The remaining **25 PDFs** are indexed for later note preparation. All 54 notes remain `reviewed: false`, and existing Human notes are preserved.

Three independent reviewers audited 18 notes each, including all 24 original notes. They checked substantive claims against exact stored sources, relevant figures, tables and appendices, all author names, metadata, tags, research groups, directed research relationships and public release scope. After a separate remediation step, they verified the final versions and recorded their hashes. No experiments were reproduced. This is a source-consistency audit, not confirmation that reported results are scientifically correct.

[Paper index](wiki/index.md) · Research groups · [Detailed provenance and findings](raw/manifest.json) · [Complete link-results table](raw/link-audit.csv)

sections.heading: Coverage and result
sections.content:
| Check | Coverage | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Note structure, metadata types, sections, filenames, paired PDFs and index summaries | 54/54 notes | Passed |
| Substantive source claims, all authors, relevant visuals, tags, groups and directed research edges | 54/54 notes | Checked, with disclosed source limitations below |
| Final-version independent recheck | 54/54 notes | Passed after corrections, exact hashes recorded |
| PDF inventory, identity and checksums | 79/79 PDFs | Original bytes preserved, no duplicate hashes or paper identities found |
| PDF-only inventory and metadata | 25/25 records | Checked, full methods not audited |
| Local navigation, filename case, headings and relevant Obsidian references | 718 occurrences, 145 resolved destinations | Passed |
| External URLs, including historical provenance | 883 occurrences, 448 unique destinations | Every unique URL requested with GET, identity assessed separately |
| Human approval and Human notes | 54/54 notes | Preserved, no agent approval substituted |

The audit enumerated **1601 link occurrences** across **63 linked input files** (70 Markdown/JSON files scanned), with **593 unique resolved destinations**. 33 intentional examples, template placeholders and historical superseded note paths were excluded. External requests were deduplicated, redirects followed, and failures retried or checked against primary alternatives. **Zero inventoried external destinations were left unrequested.** Two historical page identities remain unresolved because their contents were unavailable, as detailed below.

The CSV has one row per link occurrence, preserving source file/location, original and final destination, status, identity decision and correction or limitation. It is a generated result of the editable Markdown/JSON input snapshot, not recursively counted as a new source of links. Its destinations are the same audited set. Raw PDF bibliography hyperlinks were not exhaustively audited. Source hashes and reviewer scope are stored per paper in the manifest. Network responses reflect the check date, not a continuing availability guarantee.

sections.heading: Errors corrected
sections.content:
The independent note audits recorded **16 Errors**, **12 Warnings** and **11 Suggestions** before remediation. Detailed initial findings and final rechecks remain in the manifest. No required note-content or structural corrections remain open.

| File / section | Observed problem | Correction and evidence |
|---|---|---|
| [ExpertAF](wiki/2025-ashutosh-expertaf.md), Evidence and limits | All three human-rated outputs described as about 3.2/4 | Commentary and retrieval are 3.2/4, pose generation 2.4/4. Verified visually in Table 1 and supplement G. |
| [Ego-Exo4D](wiki/2024-grauman-ego-exo4d.md), Evidence and limits | 50.4% called the best ego-only demonstrator result without its protocol | Added single-take qualifier. Table 10 reports 51.0% with multiple takes. |
| [Ego4D](wiki/2022-grauman-ego4d.md), Authors | Six duplicated comma separators | Corrected separators. All 85 names match the source. Ego-Exo4D’s separate 101-author list also checked completely. |
| [IndEgo Assistant](wiki/2026-chavan-indego-assistant.md), affiliations and Approach | Explicit divisions/departments omitted, single-demo retrieval asserted beyond the stored paper | Restored title-page affiliations. Described direct pretrained embeddings without fine-tuning, per §§2.3 and 4. |
| [ProSkill](wiki/2026-mazzamuto-proskill.md), affiliations | IPLAB imported from project metadata into the stored-paper affiliation | Restored University of Catania as printed. Group evidence remains separate. |
| Research connections across existing notes | Newly available papers still referenced by raw PDFs, external URLs or plain titles | Replaced source-verified references with local wikilinks. No edges inferred from topic similarity. |

Warnings and suggestions also led to narrower main-topic tags, an explicit FPL reward-conditioned `rl-fine-tuning` classification, a corrected StreamArena source locator, stronger official venue links, clearer release labels, corrected register formatting and a repaired stale Obsidian reference. Publication metadata was updated for four PDF-only sources, with R4D-SG acceptance still identified as author-reported.

sections.heading: Remaining source and verification warnings
sections.content:
These are limitations of evidence or sources, not uncorrected note claims.

| Source / location | Warning | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| [Assembly101](wiki/2022-sener-assembly101.md), §5.7 vs supplement §3.4 | Prefix-only language conflicts with a window extending beyond the segment end | Preserve both descriptions, do not claim demonstrated causal online detection. |
| [DirectMe](wiki/2026-wang-directme.md), §4.1 vs Appendix D.3 | Causal processing claim conflicts with whole-trajectory offline graph construction | Explicitly distinguish intended online use from the evaluated graph. |
| [SPOC](wiki/2026-mandikal-spoc.md), dataset/evaluation | Source counts disagree and threshold-calibration split is unclear | Avoid a reconciled count or unsupported no-leakage claim. |
| [VidOSC](wiki/2024-xue-vidosc.md), dataset/evaluation | Small count differences between source versions, unclear threshold calibration | Keep exact-version caveat and the evaluated open-world definition. |
| [MATT](wiki/2026-li-matt.md), Tables 3 and 6 | PNR localization is 0.638 s in one table and 0.438 s in another | Do not choose an unverified single value. |
| [ProactEgoMem](wiki/2026-liao-proactegomem.md), Sci benchmark | Subtotals sum to 560 while abstract/table total says 500 | Avoid asserting a verified total. |
| [EgoLife](wiki/2025-yang-egolife.md), title page vs Appendix A | Corrected v3 title affiliation and stale appendix disagree for Pengyun Wang | Metadata follows the corrected title page, without adding the stale institution. |
| [FPL](wiki/2026-torne-freeform-preference.md), Table 8 vs project | Same aggregate is labeled success rate and task progress | Keep the distinction. Original Christiano implementation used A2C/TRPO, despite FPL’s historical PPO description. |
| [VidParse](wiki/2026-gupta-vidparse.md), version/venue | Stored v2 corrects GTEA to four splits, site/repository describe older settings. Conference title and first-author display differ. | Follow stored v2 for methods and author spelling. Conference page independently confirms acceptance and identifies VidParse in its abstract. |
| Timing and practical evidence | Some results omit ingestion, recognition, future context, annotation or human intervention | Retain stage-specific cost and causality caveats. FLORA cost is modeled and operational GR00T use is author-reported. Robot experiments are not proof of construction-worker skill. |

Release checks also remain qualified: MOSCATO provides dataset resources but no implementation in the inspected repository. TGML links the DTGL predecessor release, with journal additions unverified. IndEgo Assistant publishes a later reference implementation rather than its original experimental repository. ProSkill releases annotation/ranking/extraction tools. FLORA releases sample inference code rather than its production system. Missing code claims are bounded by checked sources.

The register contains 39 groups or teams, with at least one verified attribution for 40 notes. Fourteen notes remain unassigned rather than inferring teams from institutions. ProSkill’s LIVE attribution could not be independently reconfirmed, so the current note retains only Co-AI. The historical attribution remains in provenance. The CUC group uses a readable institutional leadership announcement instead of its generic homepage shell.

sections.heading: External link results
sections.content:
Final GET results: **431 HTTP 200**, **9 HTTP 403**, **3 HTTP 404**, and **5 requests without a usable response**. A 200 response alone did not count as identity verification. Browser challenges, anti-bot pages and dynamic shells are described in the CSV, with corroborating primary evidence where available.

- **Three confirmed 404s:** StreamArena’s former paper-listed website, the historical Kunyu Peng profile, and a failed candidate EgoExo4D GitHub organization. The latter two are provenance/negative-check records. StreamArena explicitly labels the former site unavailable and provides the active repository. Historical receipts were preserved rather than silently rewritten.
- **Access restrictions and timeouts:** publisher pages, ACTION Lab, Preprints.org and some institutional catalogs. Paper or group identity was corroborated through primary indexed pages, official projects or publisher-deposited metadata where possible. These results do not imply that the resources are absent.
- **Two unresolved exact-page identities:** the LIVE publication catalog and the IPLAB TGML announcement. Both timed out after retries. No current paper-to-group or venue claim depends solely on either page.
- **OpenReview browser challenges:** direct ReWiND and FPL forum requests were blocked, despite status 200. Their canonical identities and acceptance are independently corroborated by primary indexed OpenReview records.

Every occurrence, including inaccessible and historical links, is retained in [the separate CSV](raw/link-audit.csv). No unsupported replacement URL was guessed. The report is complete as an audit with recorded access gaps, not an assertion that every remote page was readable.

sections.heading: Coverage gaps and next reading
sections.content:
The added set covers the ten selected foundations and twenty complementary works. It improves the 2021–2024 lineage through Ego4D, Assembly101, Look for the Change, VIP, Ego-Exo4D, EgoPER, AMEGO, VideoAgent, OSCaR and VidOSC. Earlier Christiano and Doughty papers provide preference-learning and skill-ranking roots.

R3M, EgoVLP and CaptainCook4D remain useful reserves. Diffusion Policy, ACT and RLPD are later robot-policy foundations. Construction-specific evidence remains thinner than memory/QA and procedural benchmarks. ConstructAI’s official full text was recovered for screening but remains outside this fixed expansion. Its reported deployment and business outcomes need stronger independent validation. No additional source was inserted beyond the authorized 30 notes.

Memory/QA coverage is now dense. Further graph-memory papers should add a distinct assumption, representation or evaluation rather than another similar leaderboard result. The most useful next step is human review and a small evidence-preserving pipeline comparison, not immediate further expansion.
